The Moth, The Mountain, and the Middle-Aged-Man is a story of redemption. 
It's A story of a Universal man who says “yes” to life over and over again. 
The story of a fluid man. 
The story of an individual who lets go of certitude to find the Universal love within himself. 
The story of a man who makes peace with his feminine nature, in order to find his masculine BaCkBoNe. 
It is the story of a son who longs to make peace with his father. 
The story of fathers who long to be with their children. 
It is the story of a man who loves his Mother. 
It is the story of a Universal Snake unwinding within a man--the same snake that circles upward through his Chakras. 
It’s the story of a Universal Cat who shows the way back to the wild. 
It’s a story about the-embracing and the-letting-go of form to allow the deepening of consciousness in the individual, and the collective. 
It’s a story about going to the places that scare you. 
It’s a story about going past the point of no return. 
It’s a story about the wisdom in the mushrooms that turned the rocks into soil. 
It’s a story of the Chiefs who hold form. 
It’s the story of the ones who can’t be held by the form that the Chiefs hold. 
It’s a story about becoming Trans-Rational/Trans-Plural and integrating all the forms that had to be forsaken to get where we are today. It’s a story about a writer, an artist, a musician, and a tree Goddess. 
It’s a story of the One who simultaneously holds the suffering in one hand and the joy in the other. 
This is the story of a man who is delivered from exclusive bible-belt-fundamentalism and into the absolute openness of the Universal Christ (for a Christ who is not Trans-Universal is not Universal at all). 
It’s a story about the infinite depths of the human being. 
a story of the infinite expanse of the Cosmos. 
a story about the breath of God, the name that cannot be spoken. 

This is a story of a finger which points to the moon. 
This is a story of two shoe salesmen who arrive in a town where no one wears shoes. 
This is the story of the infinite as expressed through limited form which is transcended time and time again through the course of a lifetime. 
This is the story of letting Go. 
The story of releasing. 
Of floating. 
Of trusting 
of being. 
This is the story of experiencing rather than believing.
 This is our story of growing up. 
It’s the story of a reformed, atheist Buddhist monk who asks a man to do a miracle for himself in the rewriting of his story. 
This is the story of a man who has lost his family and his job, a man who has broken all the promises he ever made. 
This is the story of a man who has no home to call his own. 
This is the story of a man who has no righteousness of his own, but accepts the free gift of unconditional positive regard offered to him by a Universal Presence with wide open arms. 
This is the story of a 21 day real-time journey of healing as documented by the man who is on it. This is the story of the narrator who allows the story to be lived through him. This is the story of an author who chooses to die so that his reader may find new life.



Simply stated, this is a story of a man who reaches out for help…And 
this is how our story begins, with a distress call. 
It is early one Wednesday morning. Our man has just eaten some psychedelic mushrooms. 
But this time, instead of allowing himself to sink into the soil, he begins writing. 
He begins writing an email to two friends, a husband and wife who own a pubishing company. 
He wants to send them a draft of the autobiography that he has already written, but he doesn’t—he withholds—instead he starts a new story. 

A story that begins now with the sending of this email to his two new friends—his two new friends who just happen to own a small publishing company, Muse Harbor



Please pardon the draftiness, after all, it is a distress call.

Begin draft:



The middle aged man walked the chilled winter streets of a college-cow-town on the Eastern High Plains of New Mexico. The little town was not the type that most people imagine when New Mexico comes to mind. It wasn't anything like Santa Fe or Taos, those quaint cities with mountains for their backdrop where accomplished artists open up shops to sell their creations to tourists. The far East of New Mexico, while still officially a part of the land of enchantment, has much more in common with the rolls and flats of the Texas Panhandle. "The land of the scrub brush and awfully high winds," is how the middle aged man often described it. 



During his first Spring there, seventeen years ago, the sky filled with red dust and the ground bustled with tumbleweeds, some the size of Volkswagen Beetles, which rolled menacingly across Highway 70. The smaller weeds appeared to him as escaping convicts, dashing across the roads, leaping barbed wire fences to continue their manic jailbreak across the fields and over the horizon. As he drove his young family to the nearby neighboring city, he was unsure of what to do when encountering these tumbleweeds. Should he stay his course and collide with them, or slam on his brakes risking a traffic accident and the lives of his children in the back seat? 

It was often difficult to predict the path and speed of the rolling vegetation. He imagined himself to be Han Solo, navigating the millennium falcon through an asteroid field. ["No. He didn't actually imagine himself to be Han." said the writer, "but, that IS the voice that I’m making peace with here." 

literary voice {not-literal}. Fictional Autobiography {aren't they all?}... 

He was not Han solo. This particular young man was Luke Skywalker...this young man never ever imagined himself as Han, although the falcon was his dream to fly...he did love the falcon...yes there was something in this young man that loved the Falcon very much...but, this young man was Luke. 

[if I can allow myself to comment on my own draft here...is this part of the creative process? is that how this is done? this email as a part of a greater creative effort...consciousness commenting...looking back on itself?].



The truth is...that this young man had never...ever...thought of himself as Han (although, as mentioned before...he did love the Falcon)....LUKE. there was only LUKE. this young man was Luke.



but, back to these weeds...which were real...Luke is trying to manage these tumbleweeds right now...can I acknowledge Han and the falcon in all of this? what about Leia and her distress message? she’s the one who started this whole journey in the first place. Right? More about Leia later.



Ok...really...back to the weeds....the weeds on the Eastern High Plains...yes...it’s capitalized. Eastern High Plains...



He assumed some of the weeds small enough that maybe it would be no-big-deal running over them, but they were still a problem, as they caught in the grill or the undercarriage and scratched the red paint off his young family’s Dodge Caravan, the same van that would eventually catch fire at exactly mile marker four-twenty-eight on this same highway just a few weeks in this young man's future. 

The red sky, high winds, and sense of isolation on these plains made him feel as if he'd been stationed in a colony on the far side of mars. 

(The far side of mars? Mars rotation does not have the same relationship to the earth as the moon, so there’s really not a “far side” of mars. You can’t do the same with Mars that Pink Floyd did with the Dark Side of the Moon. The moon, strange as it has often seemed to me, is always...yes always facing the earth with the same side toward us. And what I’m wondering now is this: Could this anomaly somehow stand in support of the flat-earth theory? I mean, the only other planet-like object in the sky that I can see with my naked eye appears to me as a disc, not a sphere. When I first watched a flat-earth documentary I was beside myself in confusion. I kept thinking that at any moment the narrator would reveal the film as some kind of test, measuring the audience’s critical thinking skills. But the narrator did not do that, and that’s okay because it still functions as that test, even without revealing itself as such. What I’m saying is that the documentary really caused me to question myself, “What do you REALLY know about the nature of our universe that causes you to experience the earth as round? The flat earth documentary is potentially a genius tool in that respect. And it worked that way for me without the narrator having to blow the cover. In fact, maybe it’s more genius that way. Before we knock or ridicule the flat-earthers, maybe we can at least ask ourselves this question. What do I really know that causes me to believe that the earth is round? This type of thinking is going to be important as we move forward in the evolution of this story.)



Our Luke was now an middle-aged-man. Seventeen years had passed since that first New Mexico spring, and those dust storms. This slender middle-aged-man with the greying beard had recently purchased an olive-drab jacket from Wal-Mart which he felt he needed for a poorly timed and insufficiently planned hitchhiking excursion in the dead of winter. Determined to make it to Oklahoma City to visit his mother, he got only as far as the West Texas town of Amarillo. He arrived there by the generosity of a Truck Driver named Mark...and Joseph....and Brad....



After climbing down from the cab of Mark’s white semi at an Amarillo truck stop , he eventually found what seemed like a suitable on-ramp from which to beg a ride. There he sat, cross-legged with his cardboard sign on the banks of I-40. He remained there for an hour-and-a-half, in the cold, the sun setting. He waited for a ride that was never offered. Frustrated by the law that prevented him from hitching on the interstate, unable to provide his own forward momentum, he resigned to the nearby Denny's and humbly gave up his hitchhike when his younger friend Jerry called to check his well being.



“How are you, my friend? Are you okay? I’m worried about you?”



“Yeah Jerry, I think I’m done. Could you come get me?” said the middle-aged man, the miracle in all that being the man’s seamless transition from determination to surrender without any hint of self-hate (The miracles...that’s our focus here. There are no small miracles. There are no difficult miracles. They are all the same size and difficulty level, flowing from the One heart of love…this is what A Course In Miracles was teaching the middle-aged man)



Some were confused by the hitchhike attempt. His youngest daughter asked,

"Is you car broken, Dad?" 



"No," he answered, "I have just always wanted to put a pack on my pack and start walking. I was answering a Call. Trying to be true to my Self. It was the most honest expression today. It was as genuine as I could allow myself to become."



He had recently resigned his job. But, after handing in his resignation letter he found himself unable to work through his two weeks notice. It was then suggested to him that it might be appropriate for him to be placed, once again, on medical leave. He accepted that offer. With gratefulness he accepted all that was offered.

3:45AM



Dave and Eileen

Eileen and Dave



I’m starting to wonder how much I am on my own in this thing. How much time do I spend alone in this? Is it days or weeks? How much time passes? How much writing occurs on this bathroom floor before I pass it on? Do i pass on everything, or do i do some editing of my own. I’m going to pass this on now, becuase this is early stages and I really have absolutely no idea what I’m doing or if this is something that actually needs to be done. Is this going to be of benefit to anyone? Will this benefit you? Will this benefit me? Will this benefit others? Will this contribute to the Awakening? I know that I am awakening as I am writing. That is all that I can really know. That’s what I’ve experienced today. So, I’m writing this paragraph as the last paragraph for the moment, but I’m going to copy it back to the top and leave this right here in recognition of the “circle back” that Eileen wrote of in her letter to me. I’m just going to leave everything as it is. I’m no going to do any self editing right now. First of all, I’m not sure that I even understand what it was that you two recognized in the writing yesterday. So, I’m just going to leave it all and hope that I can learn through our communications what is happening here, and maybe as time goes on I will be able to see what is pertinent and what is not.

Draft:



The middle-aged man wondered, “Will God withdraw his spirit from me?” He paused. A nod to his vipassana practice. “What kind of question is this? Knowing what I know, what kind of question is this?” thought the middle aged man to himself, as he sat on the bathroom floor, his laptop perched on an old milk carton. He closed the bathroom door and ran the hot shower just to heat up the air in the small room. “How wasteful,” thought the middle-aged man. “How can I live with myself?” Samuel Barber’s Adagio for strings played in his headphones. He wondered if this track was too melodramatic for the background to his life’s story. 



(Barber’s Adagio, melodramatic? No, this music comes from the center. This music is drawn from the One Well. This is the music of the death and resurrection. This music bears witness to the BOTH AND... death and life AND that which is beyond the binary. Barber bears witness to all the lives that have ever lived and have been lived through. It is a miracle of perception. It is a miracle which allows us to see into that realm which could not otherwise be seen. It is the gospel that was preached by the Nazarene. It is the Buddha sitting under the tree. It is mother Theresa caring for the poor. It is the surrender in Jihad. It is the Universal Mother who resides in the soil, holding all of humanity. It is Ghandi being influenced by Thoreau. It is MLK holding what he held while he held it, in all the beauty of his imperfect form. It is the peak of the trip. It is the death of ourselves. It is the calm after the storm. Just because it evokes emotion does not make it melodramatic. Allow it to give you your humanity back. Allow it to speak to you what words cannot. Allow it to hold you, to love you, to become you, to be you.)



“This business of writing,” he thought to himself, “It’s really not about writing at all, is it?”



“Father?” said the middle aged man. “

“Yes, Son.” said the middle aged man.

“How will I live with myself?”



This is one of the questions that the middle-aged man asked himself often these days: “How can I live with myself?” This morning he asked this question of the Father who he recognized to reside within his own being.



“Father?” said the middle-aged man. “Yes, Son,” said the middle aged man.

“How can I live with myself, Father?”



Just the night before, the man sat in a booth with his son-in-law at a local mexican restaurant in the college-cow-town. He and the son-in-law were making an exchange. The inner pocket of the man’s olive drab jacket contained a baggie. Inside the baggie was five grams of psychedelic mushrooms. Outside the restaurant, in the son-in-laws car, there was a single tab of LSD. The man and the son-in-law sat together, talking about their most recent trips.



So when the man woke up at 3:30am the following morning he felt guilty. And this is how the man came to ask himself this question. “Will God withdraw his spirit from me?”



“Father?” said the middle-aged man. 

“Yes, Son?” Said the middle-aged man.

“How will I live with myself. My son in law’s parents would not approve. My ex-wife would not approve. Will you withdraw your spirit from me?”



The man’s consciousness hung there as Arvo Part’s Spiegel im Spiegel emanated very softly from his headphones. He sensed somehow that God had not withdrawn his spirit, that this business of living with one’s self had more to do with how willing he was to accept himself in contrast to how willing God was to accept him. 



“It is true,” thought the man, as he sat cross legged on the floor of the steamy bathroom,“writing has so very little to do with writing, and everything to do with how to sit on this bathroom floor. It has everything to do with the question, ‘How can I live with myself,’ and especially the tone with which I ask this question.” The middle aged man was a musician, for him, so much depended on tone.



He wondered what would happen if he acknowledged his Father again. What would happen if he left some space there? He had recently been witnessing miracles arising from that space.



“Father?”



And then it happened. Life opened up right before him, or rather within him. The miracle of consciousness looking back upon itself without guilt or shame, and all the inner spaciousness that comes with an experience like that.



The space between the call and response. The quiet presence before the loving Father answers the call of the Son. The Adagio for strings had returned on the man’s playlist. With every sentence that he typed he wondered if he would be able to continue in this space, this space between the call and response. 



“Yes, Son?” said the Father.



And then there was the next space. The one created after the Father responds to the Son. A space of great creative potential. And in this space the man saw a fork in the road. He witnessed the binary, the inevitable binary of human existence. “Do I go left or right? Do I take this road or that road?”



He sat cross legged on a blanket that he’d crocheted years ago. It was an odd blanket. Eleven feet wide and three and a half feet long. The man had only learned how to do one stitch, which was taught to him by his wife’s cousin, whom he had fallen in love with after she’d told him how she’d had an orgasm while listening to his music. The man had spent many hours trying to perfect this one dense stitch. He crocheted small blankets for his children and skirts for his daughter’s Barbie dolls. Finally, his stitch was consistent enough that he embarked on the impossible task of a blanket that he imagined would be able to cover his family of five as they sat on the couch, watching TV together in their home. 



But he never finished the blanket. It was never big enough to cover them . And within the memory of the blanket he’d escaped the binary for a brief moment. “Writing has very little to do with the binary,” thought the man. “Well, it has very much to do with the binary, in the sense that the fork in the road will always present itself, and the point is to wait at that juncture until the road-that-is-not-a-road appears.” He wondered how many times he could experience this miracle. “That’s a ridiculous thing to wonder,” thought the man. “Writing,” thought the man, “has very little to do with writing and everything to do with this miracle. This miracle of living with myself.” So, he continued to sit cross legged on the bathroom floor, elevated and supported by the half-finished blanket that would never cover his family, waiting for the next miracle, waiting for the next non-road to appear.



Dave had recently described to him a novel that he was writing that was centered around a musician. So, Dave was a writer writing about playing music. The middle-aged man was a musician writing about writing. And Eileen was the one who had surely blessed them both. She spoke with the voice of a Universal Mother, or Universal Sister, or maybe she just spoke with the Universal power...that’s what the middle-aged man had experienced in her voice, some kind of power that may not necessarily deserve a label. Dave was closer to her and I’m sure he heard a diversity of voices. But whatever voice it was with which she had spoke had brought with it a wave of energy that the man was now riding. Her words had come with power to the man just hours after he’d sent them his psychedelic draft. He began to weep at “I SEE you,” and today he kept close to the letter as if his life depended on it.



This is the Letter from Eileen as was recorded:



Dearest heart,



I SEE you. 



Let us both rest in that for the moment. I SEE you. I see beauty, and truth, and love, and light. I see suffering that wants to fade, and a compassionate heart willing to hospice it, for as long as it takes. I see a dream for a better tomorrow, struggling to find purchase in the frozen soil. I see the rising sun in the East preparing itself to grow stronger, warmer, steadier, and to melt the permafrost in men's heart's so that life can blossom anew. 



I see you as tender seedling, unfurling with radical trust and feeling eager to shoot through the coldness of the soil and stretch yourself openly and irrevocably toward the rising sun. 



I rise with you, my brother. I rise with you. 



And I hear you. I hear the way your soul speaks through the words that flow through you. I bear witness to the nonlinear nature of the new state of consciousness that arises, and the experience of Self lovingly, kindly and compassionately harvesting the hard-won wisdom born of ego; including it while transcending the form-limitations of self-consciousness, in order to transform the entirety of this world to a higher fractal iteration than the one we are presently experiencing. 



I love the nonlinear way you've approached this writing, and the authentic, vulnerable way you "circle back" on yourself when ego starts to raise the mask once more. I see you picking up the mask, noticing it, and putting it back down with greater awareness each time...and I LOVE the boldness and uniqueness of that format. So I wish to encourage you to create in this brand new genre—the genre of Self-awareness conversing with self-consciousness, even as they work in tandem to tell a wonderful story. (Dave likes it too, yet his focus is on powerful through line (the electrical current) while mine is on spiral dynamics (the magnetic field). Therefore, we wish, in tandem, to encourage you to write this electromagnetically "charged" expression of your unique energy, and to offer our support along the way as you discover what this radical new style brings. Dave can help you with making sure you're forging the through line in a powerful way; I can help to ensure that you create a magnetic field of attraction that draws people in. Clearly we can see that you're a wildly talented writer; that's the rare bit. Lots of people can craft (they study) style (they practice) and produce (they commit to the process). But talent? That's the fourth card, the "wild" card that makes ALL the difference in the quality of the output. 



So...my soul says "yes!" to supporting you in continuing along the present path. I want to see where this goes, and what you can do when you create from this place of cooperative, coalescing merging of formerly separate "parts" within yourself. To SHOW the world what the inner process looks like by opening up your consciousness for all the world to watch as you dialogue with yourself in real time seems a wondrous gift, and an act of immense courage. I trust you to appreciate how precious a gift this is. I sense your current willingness to take this journey of real-time self-discovery. I know you possess ample courage already to carry on with the effort, despite the challenges such an approach presents. I feel the aliveness of your self-compassion and know that will serve you well when your energy falters. I receive the kindness in your words through the way you treat yourself even when you are calling out your own bullshit, and I know that our species can learn a good deal from that process. I respect the patience with which you have been committing yourself to the task of self-realization, and my spirit receives your offering with the peaceful intentionality from which it was created. 



Let us therefore go forth and discover how this project wants to be birthed. The journey of 1000 miles has already begun. Let's take the next step together, with loving trust that all IS well as we do so. 



Much love,

Eileen



So, as the man woke that morning, this is what he felt threatened to lose. This is why he asked G_d if he would withdraw his presence. He felt that he had surely disqualified himself from the promise of yesterday by making the psychedelic exchange with his son-in-law. He gave his son-in-law three grams of mushrooms and his son-in-law gave him a single tab of LSD. 



While they sat at the restaurant, the son-in-laws parents appeared unexpectedly. They sat and ate at the same restaurant while the middle-aged man and the son-in-law discussed their latest trips. As they were being seated, the middle-aged man smiled and waved with genuine friendliness in his heart, but he could not help but detect a disconnect, or was that possibly fear in their eyes? He thought he saw some kind of horror in both of them as he now sat with their son. And so again, the man came back to himself in the bathroom, sitting in the half-lotus, faced with a right and a left turn, a fork in the road.



He knew that what he was trying to do was impossible. That’s what the miracle is, the allowing of the impossible. He knew that self-justification was pointless. And, it was just as pointless to assume that he knew what others were thinking or feeling about him. Self criticism would only take him back to the psychiatric unit. He knew that he would have to rely on Dave and Eileen to make sense of this draft; and simultaneously he was sure that it was only him that could make sense of this (and he was, as he was now reading over this draft, making revisions and rediscovering the flow that was innate in the spirit of this evolving narrative). 



He knew that he was not a writer in and of himself, and that anything that was born of this process would be the work of a trinity. A sacred three. So, he trusted. He just kept allowing this miracle to happen. Because, after all, the man knew that he was not a writer, he was a guitar player who had been to a psychiatric unit so that he could receive a prayer from a gay black man. The prayer was one of restoration, that’s all the middle-aged man remembered about the prayer. ”The Lord is restoring you,” the man had said to him. 



And now the middle-aged man had discovered that he was also a pray-er of prayers and a miracle worker. And so, he continued in his search for other miracle workers. And he began finding them. And yesterday morning he’d worked a miracle on his chromebook after eating some psilocybin mushrooms. 



The middle-aged man was not making any assumptions about the miracles, or at least he hoped that he was not. In fact, he searched his heart to discover if he was now. All that he knew for sure was that this wave of energy felt real. And the words he’d received from Eileen and Dave were life-giving.



Now, working a miracle after eating mushrooms concerned the man, because the man had been diagnosed with the disease of “more.” This disease of “more” was common, especially among people of European descent. Early in the colonization of North America, the native Americans had identified this disease as the Wetiko spirit. It is the disease that takes and takes and takes. It is the disease of the mind and heart that cannot and will not stop taking until everything is taken. So this is why the middle-aged-man was concerned for himself. Could he allow the medicine to be medicine without demanding the “more” that the medicine could not and would not give?



He had turned to the mushrooms in a moment of desperation. However, it seemed to him that it was not a move of desperation. A moment of desperation requires a move inspired from a place of stillness. And that is what had happened. The psychedelic experience had been approaching him for an entire year, ever since he’d visited the psychiatric unit in Roswell. Then he went to another treatment center after that in Rio Rancho. By principal, and in the name of his sobriety, he had resisted and resisted the Spirit which was moving him down this path psychedelic recovery. But synchronicity after synchronicity had shown him this way over the last year. 



He finally allowed himself to be embraced by the wisdom that had turned the rocks into soil. The fungus. He felt emraced embraced by the medicine that was before man. He said “yes” to the ancient method. He risked it. He was risking it now, not knowing what the outcome of this narrative would be, or how the characters would develop, but he was beginning to see that the driving force of evolution was behind him. He was experiencing a Universe that was for him. A Universe that was out to help him.



Every experience with the mushrooms he’d had since then had been life affirming. No two journeys with the mushrooms had been the same. The man’s inner wisdom created profoundly unique ceremonies for him each time, ceremonies that would never be repeated. The man had taken a picture of a framed quote hanging on the wall of a cabin where he’d taken one of these healing journeys, “There are all kinds of love in this world, but never the same twice,” F. Scott Fitzgerald. And this is how it had been for him. 



He was drawing from the Source that inspired ALL ceremony, the impetus behind the formation of all ancient religions, the inspiration for pre-historic cave paintings. He was seeing into the eternal, the ancient visions which had become the sacred arts. He had seen the Christ in the death and resurrection of a miller moth. In the Kachina dolls he had acknowledged all the chiefs of this world who had been holding form, however imperfect all these forms and their chiefs may be, and he was able to humble himself before these Chiefs, blessing them, thanking them, even offering himself, once again, to this dance-of-form in which we all participate as we dance behind these masks that we find ourselves putting on and taking off and puttting on again.



During these journeys the man saw many things. The man had seen the snake that had devoured him as a child, the snake that underlies all our being, the snake that molts and brings new life, the snake that is feared by the religious, the snake that was lifted up on the cross, the snake that was in the garden of Eden. 



The medicine helped him to feel the care and attention of the craftsman as planted in the door-frame of his bedroom. He smelled his own human body, making peace with his pungent primate odor, seeing himself as a successful expression of the evolution of all consciousness contained in his own species. He saw his own face as a thunderhead, understanding that nothing is nearly as solid as we so often believe it to be, and in this vision he understood the suffering that we bring upon ourselves by refusing to flow with the dynamic nature of being (the secret of the thunderhead). He’d stripped naked and laid on the cold damp earth in efforts to express his willingness to experience the G_d of cold and the G_d of warmth. He immersed himself in a cold mountain stream by a highway, in his underwear. He began a dialogue with a Heavenly Father as he trekked up a mountain. He agreed to participate in the creation of a new genre. He agreed to participate in the creation of novel form.



Some of these things he experienced under the direct influence of the mushrooms. Some of these actions he’d done afterwards, inspired by what he’d seen, or heard, or felt during the direct experience.



For four years now he had been attending twelve step meetings in an effort to deal with his Wetiko spirit, his ego, his selfish nature. But, what he’d seen in those meetings was that the people in the AA rooms, even the ones with years and years of sobriety had so often been unable to deal with the core of their issues themselves. They had yet to make peace with their own Wetiko Spirit. They were still wanting and wanting, more and more, they just weren’t drinking anymore. And the man found that this experience was true for himself also. 



He found himself wanting. He had worked the steps. He eventually had an authentic spiritual experience supported by the form of the twelve steps and his dear friends in those AA rooms. He eventually felt at home there, among his fellow ego-addicts. He had felt that he’d finally found his people. He was honest. He was open. He was willing. But the AA rooms, it appeared, were not big enough to hold him. 



No one and Nothing had ever been big enough to hold him.



For all his life, the middle-aged man had gone from place to place, from person to person, looking for a people, or a woman, or a stand-in-father, or a school, or a philosophy, or a religion, a spiritual practice, or a profession, a band, a song, a genre... But, he had yet to find any form that could hold him. Many times he experienced success in his search. In fact, EVERY TIME he experienced success in his search. He had discovered along the way that, as Ken Wilber says, there are many truths, and they are all true as far as their truth goes, but none of them are the whole truth. 



But this wasn’t about truth as much as it was about the primal need to be held. To be embraced. To be touched. To be immersed in some culture, or tribe, or way of being. And now, at forty five years old, this man, having left his wife and children in search of a way to care for himself, was once again riding a wave, hoping to find again, a way to be.



The middle-aged-man longed to be held. And the middle-aged man was often held. He had been held many times in his life. He had been held. He had been loved. He had been nurtured. He had been gifted. Yet still the desperation came, time after time the desperation came. He was hungry with a desperation that could not be satisfied. Was he suffering from the sins of his fathers? What was this suffering? Was it a generational curse, passed down in his genes when a father fails to love? Did it have to do with epigenetics, trauma finding expression in our genome? 



The middle-aged-man had become the father who had failed to love. He was the husband who hated his wife. He had become the one who had broken all of his promises. He had no righteousness of his own. And, by course of life and answered prayer, he had come to meet the requirements to be a disciple of Christ. He had come to hate himself. He had come to hate his mother and father. He had come to hate his wife. And his love for his children may have been translated into a hate for himself, a jealousy for them of what he could never give himself, and therefore could never truly give to anyone else, including his offspring, the most sacred and deserving people he’d ever known. The sickness had enveloped him as he became sickeningly intimate with this hate in himself time and time again.



And this is how the writer began to find a stride, sitting in the half-lotus position in the small bathroom with the door closed and the steam fading in the bathroom. He got up to turn on the shower again, filling the room with steam.



He gave thanks for the steam. He might have forced himself to feel wasteful and guilty for this pleasure, but he allowed himself this luxury, just for today he accepted it for what it was.



He especially wondered now about Dave, and how he might write about a jazz pianist. He wondered what the musician would look like, and if he had suffered in similar ways to the musician in this story. What would that read like?



As he sat back down on the half crocheted blanket, the man remembered how he’d believed for years that if he could just think all the right thoughts that he could be okay, that he could escape this sense of desperation, this Wetiko Spirit that seemed to possess him, this hunger-to-be-held, this disease of “more,” this insanity that seemed to threaten him at every turn. 



He became a student of Buddhist thought and Vipassana meditation. He sat for up to six hours a day trying to make peace with what was happening in his being, trying to make sense of the nothingness of it all. And he was always successful, until finally he was not successful any more. He was always perfectly rational until he could no longer be Reason could no longer hold him. 



Reason was not big enough to hold him. He’d devoted himself to absolute materialism, journeying to the edge of the observable universe, scraping out the insides of his soul with what appeared to be some kind of cosmic melon-baller, all in an effort to rid himself of whatever remnants of religious superstition that might have still been tormenting him. He’d found that marijuana relieved his symptoms and helped him make peace with the world, and that worked very well right up until the point that it stopped working.



It was nearly five years ago that he had first fashioned a noose. It wasn’t a long enough piece of rope to hang himself, but he tied the noose anyway. He got the instructions off the internet. This thick piece of rope had been hanging around in his studio for years. He tied the constricting loop knot. He tightened it around his neck. It felt very good. Too good. His mind was quiet with the noose around his neck, which was very frightening to the man. He loosened the noose, tried to shake it off, then he set off for his commute to work. But the tears streamed from his eyes so thickly that he could not see the road to drive. His heaving and his sobbing were so great that he had to pull over on the side of the road. He called his therapist, Penny. She told him to go to the emergency room, so he did. 



As he laid in the ER, his head in his wife’s lap, he broke down, grateful for the help which he knew he was about to receive, but which never came. He didn’t get the help because when they asked him if he had a plan to kill himself, he would not say “yes.” He knew what they wanted to hear, but he was only willing to tell them the story of how he had tied the noose, and that was not enough to get him admitted to the hospital. The man had been willing to go to the ER. He had been willing to surrender his clothes and dawn the blue paper pajamas, but he was not willing to say what he knew he had to say to get admitted to a psychiatric unit. It was after this incident that the man gave himself to the help that the pharmaceutical industry had to offer, a sickening and demoralizing experience with prescription drugs.



He visited his first psychiatrist with his wife by his side. The doctor prescribed medications that made him sleep. So, the man put aluminum foil over the window in his studio, turned the air conditioner on full blast, and went to sleep for nearly two weeks. He had lost his job, just the beginning of the deepest sleep that the man had ever known. The greatest suffering was yet to come. He was in the grips of an inescapable death of his false-self. That which was not authentic, all that was not genuine, was passing away. The snake that had eaten him as a boy was shitting him out for a glorious resurrection. Praise be to the mother of all Ophidians. Praise be to God.









The middle-aged man got up to turn off the shower, the mirrors, once again, clouded with steam. As he assumed the half lotus in front of the old milk carton, his chromebook perched on top, he wondered, “How long can I hold this form?” He knew that writers had postural issues, slumped shoulders, forward heads. He had encountered the same issues as a musician. He’d spent much of his life sitting, embracing a guitar, practicing scales and chord shapes, immersed in a world of color and shape of sound. “There’s always the body to consider, even when one’s pursuit is in the invisible realm.” (No...the middle-aged man didn’t think that. It was something else that happened...what is that thing that’s happening there? Is this where the two meet? Is this where the unlikely happens? Is this where we get to choose between didactic and authentic? Who gets to choose that? Who really has the power to choose that? Does anyone have that power? No. not one...but three? Yes possibly three have the power to choose that. Is that why Christ didn’t write? Is that why Socrates didn’t write? But someone has to sit here and write this, yes? Or do they? Is this what is called for? What does the half-lotus have to do with this? What does posture have to do with this? Does it matter to the middle-aged man that he spent eight years working in physical therapy? Does it matter that it was a job that he may have never wanted? Does it matter that it was a direction that his wife pushed him into while trying not to be pushy? Does it matter that his family needed the resources? Does it matter that it was a practical thing that needed to be done in order to expand the nursery, to buy the kids cars and pay for a more comfortable home? Does it matter that it was a very good job where the middle-aged man learned how to be with people in a deeper way? He learned to be with people who were hurting. What’s happening now is that the man had been writing for two hours, spurred on by the encouragement of Dave and Eileen (Eileen and Dave), and he was wondering about the form of all of this. Is this the space where that thing thappens? When it gets difficult? When it becomes a physical exertion to write? Where the miracle comes again, but never the same way twice? Is that why we have such a hard time with love, because we want to know it and control it and say, “this is how love comes. I know what the miracle is. I know what love looks like.” Is that why this middle-age-man suffered? Is that why the writer was suffering?”)



The middle-aged man allowed all of this to fall in around him. He allowed the narrative and the Life to become one. He allowed the self-awareness and the Self-consciousness to observe and to be observed by one another. He allowed this because this was the miracle that he needed to see. It was the way that Love showed itself in that moment. It was the miracle that rose from within, the Christ child that was born. This is the miracle that is. This is the very evolution of consciousness itself. When the narrative itself is willingly given to deconstruction. When consciousness gives itself to the death...willingly...that’s the key word here….willingness. The birth of a new genre? The impossible. This is the place where we give away willingly what every fiber of our physical being and our ego will contract and quiver so violently in order to hold on to. A new thing to be brought into this world. Who will midwife that? Can this be born of man? 



“No,” thought the middle-aged man. “This cannot be born of man. This must be born of daughter.”



Emma Kate was the name of this middle-aged man’s daughter, so that’s how IT presented itself to him. She was seventeen years old and still living at home with her mother, the man’s ex-wife. (The fork in the road. The binary. There it is again. Here’s where the miracle happens. Here’s where the middle-aged man is beginning to understand, once again rediscovering that the miracle has nothing to do with himself and that he has no responsibility to work this miracle. This is the miracle that is already happening. The miracle that was born in his daughter. This is the miracle that cannot be performed, because performance is very far away from this miracle. This is the miracle that never demands to be witnessed and has nothing to prove. This is the miracle of the draft. The man has nothing to do with performing this miracle. The miracle has everything to do with the death that this man has already died. When his friends eat the mushrooms they have “bad trips,” in other words, they face their death. But when the man eats the mushrooms he has life affirming trips. Why is this? Is this because the man has died a death? The man knows that he cannot claim the ultimate death. He understands that his ego is still intact. He understands that the deeper parts of his being are in relationship with the shallower aspects of his being, the ego, if that’s what we want to call it. He also knows how little he understands about this. He knows the death can and will come every time. That’s why sitting at the restaurant with his son-in-law, making the exchange of the hallucinogens is such a sacred experience, because with it comes a death. The relationship that he is having with his son-in-law right now is life-affirming. And he says “yes” to this antinomial experience because it contains life. The pharisees said to Jesus, “doesn’t the scripture say be HOLY as GOD is HOLY?” and Christ says, “I’m telling you today, be compassionate as I am compassionate.” upside down crosses. Pentagrams. Satan’s salvation. Redemption of the deep ophidian, the reptile brain that still (lies) in all of us. The lies that lead to redemption. The necessary lies. The folding over of the consciousness in the Vine where we are the one who crucifies the christ, and we are the Christ who is crucified. We are the risen christ? Question marks. No certitude. No. take out the question marks, read it again without the question mark. Some things just are. The folding over of the consciousness in the vine where we are the one who crucifies the christ, we are the Christ who is crucified. We are the risen Christ. But Christ does not EVER demand to be seen. That is the nature of Christ. The ONE who does not demand recognition. The cross merely points to the nature of reality. It was/is a form. Another form is coming. The second coming of the Christ in us. That which will hold the middle-aged man, and that which will hold his daughter. That which is big enough to hold those which the current form cannot hold. That is what brings new form, a need to be held. That which will hold everything. That by which everything is held. That which will hold everything that desires to be held. All life enfolded and embraced.



“Father?”

“Yes, Son.”

“Can we climb that mountain?”

“We can try, son. One step at a time.”



The man had an intuition, a feeling, a sensation before they seated themselves at the mexican restaurant, that it might be better to go somewhere else, but he controlled himself. He did not want to be too flighty. He did not want to change their course mid-stream. That was the type of behavior that his ex-wife did not approve of. He did not want to be guilty of that kind of “manic” behavior that she’d accused him of in the text message the night before. “Was it an accusation?” He wondered, “or just an astute observation born of twenty years of being together?”



Who are the manic men? Are they the ones bringing things into the world? Still? Really? What about the daughters? Are they to be raised by the women who hate the manic men? Do the manic men still have some kind of say? Or is our time over? Is it time for me to pass away? Or do I still have a place in this world too? The “i” just popped up. I don’t know the difference now. Just trying to let this happen. Are these questions important? The ego driven questions? The hurt? The anger? The resentment? Is there a place for that? How does this narrative hold that?



Yesterday the man sat in front of the laptop, on his bathroom floor, his body writhing like a snake in molt, performing a miracle after having eaten the mushrooms, God’s flesh. Now he sat in the same place, recalling, or being reminded of what that was like. It seemed that their was wisdom in the mushrooms. The wisdom that turned the rocks into soil how many millions of years ago? The man is aware that there is a literal timeline to all of this, the evolution of consciousness, and he is aware that the consciousness of the mushroom is born somewhere along this timeline. There are so many spelling errors. So many backspaces as the miracle continues.



What are we looking for? Is it the miracle of a book. If it’s true that there is a “brand new genre” being born here then I cannot be responsible for bringing this miracle in. Surely you know what those kinds of words will do in the being of a human. But, it’s been done before, right? The new genre? The new novel(ty). The voice that has not been heard, or at least the voice that has not been forgotten. (It’s just a miracle, right? What’s a miracle for the resurrected. Miracles are the currency of the spirit? Ha! Did i just do that. Did I monetize spirit?) The voice which we are all reminding each other, over and over again as we wake up to the true true nature of reality.



What happens when a middle-aged white man receives the restorative prayer of a gay black man at the Sunrise Mental Health Hospital in Roswell, NM. Is that fair to call this being that did the praying a “gay black man?” is that what he was? Was he a gay black man? Is this where the miracle happens? It does have something to do with being gay? Doesn’t it? It has something to do with being black? With being a woman? It has something to do with receiving a message from the blackness. From the gayness. From the woman-ness. The Christ that is masculine but carries the feminine spirit. The man who gives birth on a cross. The woman who gives birth to the man. 



“By your stumbling the world is perfected”

Sri Aurobindo



This is the great stumbling. This is the genre of the stumbling. The genre of the humbling. The genre of no genre. The formless genre that has already been created but is still being rediscovered (in me? In you?). The genre that respects and disrespects all the genres that have come before. The genre that will not be held. The genre that refuses to be categorized but that must be written. “How does one set out to write a book that will never be bound between two covers? How does one approach a publisher with a book that will not be published. How is it that two publishers would say yes to a book like that?”



These are the questions that the man sat with, in the half-lotus, on half of a crocheted blanket.

# Day 2

6:18AM



The writer was now wearing a stocking cap and the olive drab jacket that he’d bought at wal-mart in preparation of the poorly planned hitchhiking trip. He left the steamy bathroom earlier that morning to give a friend a ride to work. It’s not that his friend really needed a ride to work, it’s just that his friend was walking to work in the cold, and the man had discovered this, and so he’d offered the ride. The friend accepted, not because he needed the ride, but because he thought it would be nice to spend a little time with the man before work. And so it went. The middle aged man was just then sitting back down to write after offering his friend, who really needed no ride, a ride. 



This friend that he’d picked up because he did not need a ride was one of the friends that the man had shared his mushrooms with. After eating the mushrooms, his friend had a death-of-false-self experience. He was accepting of it. The two of them sat in the Wal-Mart parking lot, discussing their most recent experiences with consciousness, making an exchange. After the man had dropped his friend off at work, the middle-aged-man went by the donut shop, came home then sat down, once again, in the half-lotus. 



He waited for another miracle. Or rather, he accepted the miracle that had already happened and the miracle that already was in progress. “That’s what it is, really,” thought the man, “Life is just one really long miracle.”



How does the middle-aged man start writing again, after being told that he is a “wildly talented writer.” How does a middle-aged man make peace with that? How did the Christ heal the sick and remain humble? Is that why the Christ showed up in the temple one day, with a whip and some self-righteous indignation? (It’s just a story. Just a story? How can there be any “just” when referring to a story? We are made of story? Are we not? Maybe not) Is that why the Christ never wrote a book? There’s no book of Christ in the bible. Is that what we are bearing with-ness to here (Bayo Akomolafe...a young Nigerian)



How will we make any sense of this? When will I come back to the narrative? Is this where Dave’s “electrical current” comes in to play? And what about Eileen’s magnetic field? What about that. The attraction.



The middle-aged man could not be held by any form...That’s where we were...yes…



When the middle-aged man was twelve years old he knew that he was gay. Although that statement can only be partially true. Why is that? Because one lesson that the middle-aged man had learned along his way was that sexuality is very fluid, at least HIS sexuality. And just like the rest of this uncontainable being, as he had tried to nail his sexuality down in one place or another, there was an illness that came. The illness that comes when a dynamic world is reified. 



Reification was explained to the man like this by his friend, Ed, the Marxist: “You see that thunder cloud reaching high up into the atmosphere? Do you see how the sun is reflecting on one side and the other side is held by shadow? We think that’s a thunderhead, don’t we? But that’s not what a thunderhead is. A thunderhead is the sum of its lifespan and possibly the lifespan of every thunderhead that has ever existed. That thunderhead is in relationship with every other changing weather pattern that is occurring right now in our atmosphere. That thunderhead is the ocean. That thunderhead is more than we can see or comprehend with our eyes in this moment. That thunderhead is all the shapes it has been in the past and all the shapes it will be in the future. And that thunderhead is still the thunderhead after it is gone. But, when you remember this moment and try to talk about reification, it’s that image of the thunderhead that’s going to come to you first. And what you do with that image from there, well, that’s up to you and (your) novel(ty).” Ed was one wise Mexican-American.



So, that’s how you write the book that can’t be written. You hold the form. You move in and out, and you rely on those who are holding their own form, like Ed. You let go of the form. You acknowledge the impossibility of all of this. You make peace with yourself after you have done the un-thinkable...after you have disappointed yourself and all your expectations about who you think you are or should be. And you just keep typing….





And not JUST typing. But keep reading. And keep opening yourself up. Keep holding the form and letting go of the form. Willingness to participate in the form. Willingess to see that there is NO form that can hold you. Even this body, this form that you are so attached to, will one day sing its final hymn, dance its final dance, write its final poem, receive its final kiss, speak its final words, beat its last blood, shit its last shit. So, this is a story about dying. And, of course, not JUST of dying, but the reincarnation that comes after and with and because of the death. Become the incarnated resurrection. This is what is meant by the acceptance of the Christ into ones’ heart. The Christ is the seed that willingly falls into the soil in order to bring forth the tree. The Christ is the ONE who goes into the unknown without resistance. The Christ is the ONE who dies well. The Christ is the ONE who uses the whole buffalo. The Christ is ALL we can see and ALL we cannot see. You know that now. You know that the Christ is not one who can be contained in any old wine skin. The Christ is not one that can be contained by Christianity. The Christ is not one that can be believed in. The Christ can only be experienced. The Christ can only be known by embracing the sufferings, by lowering the resistance to what-is, and then saying yes to the re-incarnation of being, as we allow that Oneness to arise from Center. Christ is our experience when we stop acting compassionate, and we surrender to Compassion itself. When we die to our best patience-act and we become the Patience. When we allow that to flow from our center which we have failed to manifest by strength of our own ego, while patiently and lovingly allowing the ego (flesh) to be integrated, folded in, folded over, like blueberries in a batter. When we acknowledge those shallow (ego) aspects of our being as being shallow, but we also do not exclude them, because it is only the shallower aspects of our being that are exclusive by nature. This is why religions become exclusive, because they are run by the shallower aspects of our being. We are afraid to lose control of ourselves, so we establish these “safe” places (which include buildings and thought structures etc) in which we dwell. “Safe” in quotation marks. They are only safe as far as we can throw them. Because, as they may provide a somewhat controlled environment, a controlled environment is not necessarily where growth is going to happen. The controlled environment may be a place for a new life to incubate, but not necessarily a place where life can come into its fullness. This is how we do a disservice to those of us who wake up, when we try to insist that they stay in the incubator. Imagine a dozen chicks trying to grow up in an incubator. Ridiculous. Or crushing. Or just very sick. And sad.



But sad is okay. It’s okay to see that. To know that. To have been that. To have done that. To have experienced that. And it’s also okay to wake up to a deeper reality. It’s okay that we are suffering. It’s okay to accept that suffering in others. It’s okay to see suffering in others even when attacked.



The middle-age-man took a walk as the sun was rising. He had eaten mushrooms the night before...



So what now….



I’m starting to wonder how much I am on my own in this thing. How much time do I spend alone in this? Is it days or weeks? How much time passes? How much writing occurs on this bathroom floor before I pass it on? Do i pass on everything, or do i do some editing of my own. I’m going to pass this on now, becuase this is early stages and I really have absolutely no idea what I’m doing or if this is something that actually needs to be done. Is this going to be of benefit to anyone? Will this benefit you? Will this benefit me? Will this benefit others? Will this contribute to the Awakening? I know that I am awakening as I am writing. That is all that I can really know, is what I’ve experienced today. So, I’m writing this paragraph as the last paragraph for the moment, but I’m going to copy it back to the top and leave this right here in recognition of the “circle back” that Eileen wrote of in her letter to me. I’m just going to leave everything as it is. I’m no going to do any self editing right now. First of all, I’m not sure that I even understand what it was that you two recognized in the writing yesterday. So, I’m just going to leave it all and hope that I can learn through our communications what is happening here, and maybe as time goes on I will be able to see what is pertinent and what is not. 



This is not a book I’m trying to write here. This is (my) (our) (THE) salvation. (I )am coming to terms with what it means to live a resurrected life. (I) am coming to terms with what it means to have LIFE lived through me. (I) am crossing over the threshold, into the second half of (my) life. The container has been built. Now it is about CONTACT and CONTENT. 



I acknowledge both of you as I humbly submit this second day of writing. I am a student, trying to find the school.
