# Day 2 continued





The middle-aged man, who’d risen from his bed at three-thirty AM and typed until eleven with only one break was pleased with the work that he’d done. He took a hot bath, watched some Netflix (Living With Yourself with Paul Ruud). He swept and mopped the kitchen floor. He cleared and cleaned the kitchen counters. He emptied, scrubbed, and reorganized the shelves in the fridge. Emptied the trash twice. He ran the dishwasher and started some pinto beans in the crock pot on high heat. 



He tried to remember exactly how long he’d been on medical leave. “Let’s see,” thought the middle-aged man, “today is the twentieth of December. My last day of work would have been December 19th (the day of the Christmas party) if I would have completed my two weeks notice. So just about two weeks now I’ve been off work,” the middle aged man concluded.



The middle-aged man lived with his friend and AA sponsor, Dan G. He’d been there with him for well over a year now. Dan’s house was an impressive Southwestern style adobe structure with a koi pond in the large backyard (the kois were dead), all hemmed in by substantial evergreens. However, the backyard had become less attractive since neither Dan nor the middle-aged man cared much for yard work, especially the high level of attention that the landscaping at this home required.



The middle-aged man had now taken his half-lotus to the head of his bed where he sat propped on two pillows with his chromebook perched upon a A Course In Miracles, Volume One. He breathed deeply and waited for his miracle to happen again, listening to the cars on highway 70 and his mac pro thinking on the desk. His fingers curled comfortably over asdfjkl;. Trying to recall the lesson of the day, he got up to get the course in miracles workbook.



Having retrieved the book, the middle-aged man settled again with the chromebook in his lap.



A Course in Miracles, Lesson 6:

“I am upset because I see something that is not there.”



What was that thought he’d had this morning? He got up to get his journal. He settled again. This is what he’d written in his journal:



When the laws of man

Encroach over

His natural rights

There is disconnect 

This is a “sin” against man



He wondered if he was becoming a Libertarian. Of course he was. He’d already become everything else, why not a Libertarian.



He heard the crunch of gravel in the driveway and then voices. It was Dan and his girlfriend, Christy. A key turned in the door. Dan was a jovial man who was famous for his laugh. He heard footsteps on the stairs and then their voices disappeared as the middle-aged man continued writing.



A jet flew overhead. His mac was still thinking on the desk.



The Libertarian journal entry was in the context of his feelings about the hallucinogen exchange that he’d made with his son-in-law the night before. He was still anxious about what might happen if his ex-wife discovered this secret. He related to this anxiety in the context of lesson 6: “I am upset because I see something that is not there.”



Workbook exercise:

“I am worried about ________ because I see something that is not there.”



“What am I seeing that is not there?” the man questioned himself.



“Father?” 

“Yes, Son?”

“What am I seeing that is not there?”



“Nothing that is real can be threatened.” and “Nothing that is unreal exists.”

He now had the first lesson of the course in miracles memorized and it came to the forefront of his mind.



And then, a review of lesson 5: “I am never upset for the reason I think.”



Dan and Christy laughed and joked upstairs. They both worked in the public school system and today was their first day of the holiday break. Dan was singing a song to Eli, the cat in a high pitched voice that he had reserved just for him. Dan and Christy descended the stairs. The front door open and closed. Joyful banter in the driveway. Car doors shut. Gravel crunched. Dan and Christy were off to who knows where. They were almost always together.



Four years of AA had made the middle-aged man suspicious of himself. Four years of showing up to meetings and saying, “I’m an alcoholic”. It had been a dissonant chord for him because he never really struggled with an alcohol addiction exactly. But he could identify with the core disease, which in the AA “big book” is identified as selfishness and self centeredness. He related to the 12 steps in terms of the ego problem and he had worked the steps accordingly. 



Eli jumped up on the bed and stared. “Hey, bud.” Said the middle-aged man with the beard. “qs njp]” Eli walked across the keyboard and took up a purring position on the other side. The man straightened his cramped legs. The man stroked his lengthening beard, waiting for whatever miracle was to come. He enjoyed the miracle that was already happening. He leaned against the wall and breathed, waiting for the fork in the road to present itself. He wondered why the mac was so thoughtful tonight. “It must be updating,” he thought to himself. “Or possibly plotting.” A small smile came across the man’s face, the smile that he now referred to as the Buddha smile. The smile that exists free from any particular event. Or maybe it was the thought of his mac plotting against him that had brought the tiny smile to his face.

The course in miracles states that there are no difficulty levels in miracles, so a Buddha smile must be the same level of miracle as turning water into wine. All miracles are equal. And “miracles are natural, if they are not happening then something has gone wrong.” Thank God for the Buddha smile that originated B.C.



The middle-aged man wondered, “Am I justifying my actions with my Libertarian thinking?”



Eli got up, jumped off the bed, and left the room.



“What is threatening me? Who is threatening me? Who is this (me) that I keep referring to? And if nothing real can be threatened then maybe this “me” is the one that is not real. The man had a phrase for this: “i is not getting what i wants.” This is how he referred to his ego, the little “i”.



The man was pleased with this conclusion. And then he became immediately suspicious of the conclusion. “Resolutions. Conclusions. Certitude.” Thought the man, “Pema has taught me that none of these are sufficient. These are illusions that I create. These resolutions. These conclusions. They are less than my birthright as a human being. As soon as I think I’ve got it all together, I’ve already fallen apart.”



And so it went for the man as his posture deteriorated in front of the chromebook. He accepted the miracle for exactly what it was and he went to check the beans that he could now smell from the kitchen.



The man witnessed the miracle of his clean kitchen. The man smelled the miracle of the boiling beans. He tasted them, still not quite soft enough. 



11:32 PM December 20th





After eating some beans and a salmon fillet cooked in an oiled skillet with salt and pepper, the man exchanged texts with two friends. Then he hopped in his little blue toyota and drove half way across the college-cow-town to visit with Ron and Joann. Sherry and Stretch were just leaving as he was arriving. The three talked, standing out in the cold night for quite some time. Sherry was installing blue christmas lights on her house. Stretch was obviously pleased at the glowing blue hood ornament he’d recently installed on his cherished primer gray vehicle. Blue lights all the way around.



The middle-aged-man peaked in through the front window of his friend’s house. Joann was resting with her eyes closed on the couch. She’d been having difficulty sleeping recently. The man texted Ron again, questioning whether or not it was appropriate to disturb Joann’s rest. Ron came out on the front porch and assured the man that it was okay to come inside. Joann was not someone that the middle-aged man wanted to disturb. She carried a certain authority that he recognized and did not wish to transgress.



The man entered Ron and Joann’s home, an artist’s temple, walls yellow with smoke and the air always heavy with the smell of hand rolled cigarettes. Life’s sacred art occupied much of their living space, prophecies of an aging couple. A nude painting of Joann. A kong-sized cracked-skinned amulet. Ron’s Dark street-light-corner painting. Guitars in mid-repair. A wildly colored coffee-table-altar. A lit candle. A water bong. Books stacked horizontally on a shelf. One of the books was Joann’s favorite entitled There’s Nothing Wrong With You. She’d never read it. The woman’s twisted art, fully constructed from discarded items, hung in congregations throughout the living room, or sat in small tribes on every surface, singing homage to the practical, yet therapeutic, nature of their presence in Joann’s life. Praise be to the mother who formed the ALL, and praise to the beings who crafted this sacred living space.



The man experienced the peace of Home within these walls many times. Ron and Joann’s dwelling had always been open to the man, except once, recently, when the mushrooms that he’d shared with Ron had provided a challenging experience, what some might call a bad-trip. The texts after that night looked like this:



Middle-aged man: How’s it going?



Ron: Honestly Travis, I tripped hard for 6 hours last night, and it wasn’t good. I can still feel it a bit now, and I am extremely fragile. Give me a day or two and maybe I can talk about it, but for right now I am in reclusive recovery mode. Hope you are doing well.



Middle-aged man: okay, bud.



Ron: Love you





Middle-aged man: Love you Ron. I apologize if I brought something negative into your life. I felt lead to share, but I’m sorry you had a bad trip.



Ron: You were trying to share something that had been very positive for you. Don’t feel bad.



Middle-aged man: Peace to you. I’ve read that even the challenging trips can bring something positive into one’s life.



Ron: Oh yes, I gained some humility and some difficult insights.



Middle-aged man: I will take some deep breaths with your well-being in my heart. I love you Ron. I was up most of the night as well.



The next day…



Middle-aged man: I am thinking about you today. I acknowledge the part I played in your recent challenging journey. I acknowledge that I may not have attended to that situation appropriately. I care for you so much Ron. I accept that I may have led you down an inappropriate path or that maybe I did not provide the appropriate support. I am deeply humbled and I ask for your forgiveness in a situation that I do not yet fully understand.



Ron: Don’t worry Travis. I am ok. I think I just misunderstood and thought I was “micro-dosing” and wouldn’t trip. But I also knew it wasn’t clinically controlled, so I shouldn’t have assumed that. Joann was fairly upset with both of us, so if anything you might want to apologize to her. Otherwise all is well, but we are turning away visitors for a few days.



Middle-aged man: Wow. Okay. I understand. I will pray about how to make amends to Joann. I am willing



The middle aged man then texted Joann…



Middle-aged man: I apologize for introducing something unwelcome into your home. Please let me know how I can make things right between us. I hope to have an opportunity to earn your trust again.



Joann: The substance itself is not unwelcome. But apparently I have a little different philosophy. In my mind it is a thing not to be done lightly but with forethought and respect. Otherwise it can simply be an escape and as such can be dangerous and fruitless. I know you intended no disrespect and I don’t mistrust you. I look at it as an error in judgment or misunderstanding that can happen between friends. I do look forward to seeing you again soon.



Middle-aged man: It is my intention to treat the loving intelligence that we find in plants and fungus with the greatest respect. I acknowledge the wisdom in your words, Joann. I trust that I will learn the lesson that is to be had from this experience. I am deeply humbled. Life is a good teacher. You are a good teacher. I am grateful for you in my life.



Joann: We all learn from each other



And so it went…



The Middle-aged man had visited Ron and Joann briefly twice since then, but had not quite settled back in. He was working through some guilt surrounding Ron’s bad trip. But, tonight, he somehow felt at home again.



The middle-aged man shared his good news: that he’d made contact with a small publishing company, two friends, who had expressed an interest in his work. Word for word, he read the email from Eileen, those words that had provided so much hope and direction and energy for the middle-aged-man:



…”I see you...I rise with you, my brother…

I hear you transcending the form-limitations of self consciousness…

 Nonlinear…

 Circle-back….

 putting down the mask…

Boldness...

 uniqueness…

 brand new genre of self-awareness conversing with self-consciousness…

 Electrical-current…

 Through-line….

 Spiral dynamics…

 Electromagnetic Field…

 …we encourage you in tandem…

 …wildly talented writer…

 my soul says “yes!”...



Create from this place of cooperative coalescing…

the merging of formerly separate parts within yourself...

open your consciousness for all the world to see...

journey of real-time self-discovery….

I trust you to appreciate what a precious gift this is...

I know you possess ample courage...

I feel the aliveness of your self-compassion…

this will serve you when your energy falters...

our species can learn a great deal from that process...

the patience with which you’ve been committing yourself to the task of self-realization… 

my spirit receives your offering with the peaceful intentionality from which it was created...

The journey of 1000 miles has already begun...let’s step together…



The writer sat with Ron and Joann in this safe and sacred space that they’d established. As he sat with his friends he was also aware of the energy channeled in Eileen’s communication (The energy of Dave and Eileen). It was this wave of energy that he received in this communication that he was now riding as he sat there in a gliding rocker, conversing with his friends. It was with great joy that he had read this letter aloud. He relished every word. He had received a communication from the Source. 



As he sat in conversation with Joann and Ron (yet another communication from the source) he couldn’t help but look forward to getting back home and writing. He felt an excitement, as if he was a young musician again, and had a music engagement coming up:

The young man was seventeen years old when he got his first paying gig at the Diamond Ballroom in Oklahoma City. He walked across the enormous dance floor, carrying his red fender bass in its case, wearing his ostrich skin boots and his blond straw stetson, praise be to the great Ostrich Mother and the wheat grass descendents. The young man reveled in the thought that he was now a professional musician, getting paid to play.



The gig, however, went quite terribly. At their audition they had played their best five songs for the club owner. They were well rehearsed on those five songs especially. But, by the time the Friday-Saturday engagement arrived, West Of City was sadly out of practice. By the end of their second set they were running dangerously low on material, with still two sets to go. Midway through the third set, the boys wearing cowboy hats on stage panicked (or maybe it was just the bass player who panicked!). Under Cad’s direction, they tried to play Lynyrd Skynrd’s, Gimme Three Steps unrehearsed. An absolute train wreck. The crowd jeered, “Get a band!” “You suck.” The young man’s parents recorded the entire incident on video. The young man watched it only one time. That was enough.



But, that is not where he was right now. He was not on stage failing in front of a crowd. Right now he was safely embedded in the fabric of community. He was embraced in the loving arms of Christ as he sat in the sanctuary created by these two people who loved him. His experience was that they loved him. It wasn’t just something that they said. He had received true love and acceptance and care from these two people, these two very caring, and very human human-beings.



The middle-aged man was at ease sitting in his favorite rocking chair at Ron and Joann’s house. As he was still intentionally trying to make peace with his story, the middle-aged-man began to share from his heart. He shared with Joann and Ron recollections about his twenty year marriage:



The man watched his ex-wife (the mother of his children) scratch and claw her way through school. She was a workhorse, staying up until 2 and 3AM many nights of the week to finally get her masters and then her doctorate. Her hair started falling out. Literally. During those years she suffered a drastic hair loss. The man watched his wife trade her life for what she pursued. He watched her make the trade. It was unlike anything he’d ever witnessed before (an observation that was far from true, because he had also seen this happen in his own mother, as he was a child. A woman rising up from under the waves of oppression that had crashed down on all her sister’s that had come before her. Trying to save her own life while fighting for the survival of her family. Yes. He had seen this before).



The clicking of keys was the sound of her.



She stayed up into the early hours and did her work, surviving on coffee and the meatiness of a brutal work ethic which she’d inherited from her family. The Clarks, her people, were determined, smart, and Christian. Their denomination did not allow for musical instruments. When the young musician had first asked the woman to coffee, she was excited. The young man wasn’t an especially bad-boy, but he was the baddest boy she’d ever had coffee with. The young man who played bass and sang his newest songs of salvation in the church band.



This is what the woman had witnessed. She had witnessed the young man come alive in song as the hope of a new day coursed through him. She was witnessing the birth of the Christ. And this is who she would say yes to. She said yes to a hopeful young man who was rising up out of the depths of his fear to see life in a brand new way. She was witnessing the birth of Love and Life in this young man. And this is what she would say yes to. This is why the man had the honor to witness all that he did now. This is where their children came from. It was this awakening in the young man’s life and in the awakening of this young woman from which so much life would flow (I’m not able to express this whole picture and it is grieving me. I am determined to see. Can I move on from here for the sake of the entire draft. Can I move on, acknowledging that the immensity of all of this has not been expressed? Can I move on, understanding that I do not carry her story now. I cannot carry her story now. It is hers she must carry it. I carry the memory of her with me. Can I acknowledge the complexity of this situation in this way, and move on now? I make myself available to return here in good time).



“Do you know how much I have sacraficed for this family?” his ex-wife would eventually ask. At some point the woman’s intellect recognized that her question was problematic (problematic: a word used among English professors), but the man was never quite sure that his wife’s heart had ever recognized the real problem there. 



This is how it went: She became strong. He became weak. As she ascended to the top of her form, his form fell apart. This was not her fault. It was not his fault. It was an agreement that they had made, an unconscious understanding of which they were, in the beginning, unaware. An agreement born of lack: lack of experience, lack of knowledge, lack of heart, Lack of love. Was it the sins of the fathers being passed down to their sons for seven generations? And what about the daughters? What about the father who passes his sin on to his daughter by way of force. Now the bell rings...the metal clangs. The thing has been said. Her story is now my story.



Freud knew about this. He discovered how common incest was. He knew how common it was that a man sought comfort in his daughter (what is he seeking comfort from? And is it comfort he seeks? Or is it a willful expression of his own patriarchal dominance? Is it willful violence? Or is a subconscious manifestation of the trauma that was born in him? Surely it is unconscious. How can we know?). And Freud also knew that it was most common in the strongest of families, where the patriarch was most at ease in his world. Freud knew it. Freud said it. And then Freud revoked it, because it was too much. It was too much for him. It was too much for his world. It was more than he could bear. It was more than his reader could bear. But then he did something else. He turned it all on the “hysterical” woman (was it Freud who did this? Or was it just the macro-ego of his time made manifest in Freud? How can we know intimately the complexities of these matters?) Can you hear the grinding? The clashing of metal, or something like that? Is it just me? 



But that’s all okay now. Can I make that okay now, because I don’t have to live with it anymore? Can I call it the evolution of consciousness? Can I do that? Can I just make that okay for right now? Even though it never became okay between us. That never got “okay” in their marriage. The trauma was present. The trauma was known intimately. And it was never absorbed back into the great mother earth, because that was not a known practice to them. 



In fact, it was the Great Mother whom the woman had always longed to connect with, the one from whom she believed herself to be alienated from. Why? You may ask, dear reader. Trauma. The simplest answer is this: trauma? Generational trauma stored in soul and the unwinding of epigenetic material, this trauma that still found expression in the Daughter, the one who had never been truly held by Mother. Why was she not held by mother? You may find yourself asking again. Trauma, dear reader. Trauma. Unresolved trauma prevents the mothers and the fathers from holding their children. And this is the way that it goes...until. Until one generation finally has just enough support to put their foot down and say, “NO! This stops here. This trauma will not be passed down to the next generation. This stops here! Dear God, please let this stop here.”



Several months before, (On September 22 2019 to be exact), the text exchange between the man and the ex-wife (the mother of his children) was recorded precisely like this:



Woman: Glad you were able to come out to the Williamson Ranch on Friday. Just wanted to give you a heads up. I’ve decided that I’m going to start dating women. Not really dating yet but I have told close friends and am talking to someone. Want you to know in case word gets around.



Middle-aged man: (in the produce section at Wal-Mart): Okay. Thank you. I wish you the best, always.



Woman: same to you



Middle-aged man: I really enjoyed being around all of you on Friday. I have no expectations, but I hope that we can do it more. I would like to be included in as many family events as possible. I was grateful for the invitation from Emma.



Woman: I think it could be possible



Middle-aged man: I truly hope that we can be friends. I think it would be good for me. I think it would be good for the kids. No expectations. No pressure. This has been in my heart for months, and I’m just taking this moment to let it be known to you. I’d like to be able to celebrate the family that we spent so much time and energy raising.



Woman: I think we are moving in that direction. I’m grateful for the time we had with the kids. Friday was a good first step. Maybe we could try again when Joseph comes home for his fall break.



Middle-aged man: Great! Are the kids aware of your decision?



Woman: yes, they have known since I first decided...around June



Middle-aged man: Thanks. I just didn’t want to assume.



Woman: you are free to share with whoever. I don’t really care who knows...just not making any public announcement



They never did get together during Joseph’s fall break.



Praise be to the ONE who delivers us from bondage. Praise be to the Mother who gives her life in childbirth (they all do). Praise be to the clanging of metal against metal, iron sharpening iron. Let it all be folded in.







Early in their marriage, when their oldest daughter was just one year old, the man and the woman agreed together to sell all their possessions, inspired by the story of the rich young man in the bible who approaches the Christ, saying, “Lord what shall I do?” and the Christ says, “Sell all your shit, son. Give your money to the poor. See what happens.” 



The young couple proceeded to follow this example. One afternoon, they put the daughter in the car seat and drove their white Pontiac to the Sonic in Wynnewood, Oklahoma. There, they bought two large limeades for the parents and one small slushie for the only daughter. The young family drove home with the drinks in their laps. They did not drink them. In the green winter wheat field, they poured the sweet drinks out as an offering to the Lord. They didn’t drink the sweet drinks, you see. They poured them out. As an offering to the Lord.



The fathers were scared (sacred)...terrified of the young couples’ decision to sell and give. The terror turned into anger and manifested itself in the young man’s father. “Are you sick son? Do you have cancer? What the hell are you doing? What the fuck’s going on!?” The fathers’ voice trembled at first and then raised incrementally with each question, each interrogation containing a more demanding violence than the one before. 



It was dark and raining when the son slammed down the receiver on the land line at the farmhouse. Hurt and confused by his father’s violent reaction, he ran outside, into the storm, fell to his knees, clutched the soaked soil and tore the grass and the roots in his hands. His tears mixed with rain and mud. The son did not forsee this attack coming. He did not understand the generational curses with which he currently was fucking with. He was not wise enough. He was not experienced enough (Ahhh Jimi Hendrix…Are You Experienced? This was the experience that was now rising from within).



The young man’s father-in-law offered to send his son-in-law to a school of ministry. “The devil is roaming about like a roaring lion, son. He would just love to devour a young family like yours.” His father in law had never spoken of the devil before that he was aware of. Not quite like this at least. In such personal tones. 



“No, thank you, said the young man. I am going to follow the Christ’s calling for my life.”



“Son, we’ll send you to a bible college where they can help get all this in perspective for you. That’s what you need. Son, you’ve got a calling on your life. Let us help you answer that call. The devil. He’s gonna chew you guys up. He’s gonna spit you out on the floor. He’s gonna fuck what’s left of the remnants with his steaming cock, son! He’s gonna drag his steaming devil cock over your family whose chewed up in his saliva and he’s going to mock the very day you were born. Do you hear what I’m saying to you. Do you know what that’s going to feel like, son. Come to your senses, boy. You are going to fucking die! And your family is going to pay the price for this silly little fucking game you are playing. Son. Come to your senses.” 



The mother-in-law was the only one who had a real blessing for them. She was silently happy for their decision. The middle-aged-man remembered this. And she spoke of love and life. She prayed that God’s will would be done. She gave them this gift. It was all she could afford. It was the gift she had been dying to give. He was the son-in-law that she loved. He knew that she loved him. And he was as grateful as he could be.



The young man’s own mother was mostly silent and confused. She was, no doubt worried, as she was surely worried for the middle-aged man now as he continued to struggle. The middle-aged-man, the budding writer who sat at Ron and Joann’s recounting these stories. The one who tells stories, yet attempts to remain rooted in the NOW and the HERE.



Throughout the course of the evening, Ron and Joann held space for these stories as they came to the middle-aged man. After delivering his good news and reading the email from the publishers, he began to allow some of his hurt surrounding his relationship with his ex-wife to come up (as was his intentional practice to reconcile himself to his pain in community). 



He could feel the hurt right there in his chest, not overwhelming, but not at all comfortable. He allowed the tenderness to surface there, like a buoy on the sea of his being, as Ron and Joann held that space in their sacred home.



After describing his grief to Joann and Ron, and while still holding this discomfort in his chest the middle-aged man described what it was like recently, to be held by the Father in the midst of the great loss, to be held by the Universe, to be held by the One, the Source, Spirit, Love. He described how he had felt so alone and disconnected evn before he had left his wife and family nearly twenty one months ago. In fact, it was this sense of isolation that spurred the great Walking-Away. 



As he sat in the gliding rocker, in the presence of his two friends, he described what it was like to be married to a woman who could not hold him. What it was like to be unable to hold and comfort a woman who was averse to Man. What it was like when he was told, by his ex-wife, to get to work or get the hell out. What it was like when he had suggested a separation during a counseling session and how she had exploded, called him names, and vowed never to return to couples counseling again. What it was like when she had told him that if he ever called her “controlling” again that she would divorce him. What it was like to become weaker and weaker as she got stronger and stronger. What it was like to have a penis in a relationship where penises were only dirty-phallus. What it was like to want to kiss a woman, but not that woman who hated to kiss. Oh! the hardness of her lips! What it was like to make love perpinducularly so that the woman did not have to look into the man’s eyes. What it was like to perform unrequited oral sex dozens and dozens of times because that was safer than sex for her. What it was like to tire of the passionless “other.” What it was like to watch a woman try to climax as if it was a chore. What it was like to withdraw from her intimately, understanding that she did not EVER need or EVER want sex, or kissing, or to be looked in the eyes. What it was like to come back to her for the intimacy that his body and soul so desperately needed but could never ever receive. And finally, what it was like to go a year without sex while she was trying to process through her sexual abuse.



Ron and Joann were good friends. There truly was a dialogue between the three of them that night, but it was not recorded in any way in the writers being (not that he could detect now at least). That night at Joann and Ron’s house was a night that the middle-aged-man released some of his trauma. He had learned over the years how to release a little bit at a time as casually as he could, a lot like Andy Dufresne in the movie Shawshank Redemption.



Andy Dufresne, a wrongfully interned prisoner, is tunneling out of his cell with a little rock hammer—a rock hammer so skillfully smuggled in by his friend, Red. Every day, Andy chips away at the wall in his cell, and every day he releases the debris into the prison yard. Every day, he drops a litle bit of rock and dust right down through his pants. 



And that’s exactly how the middle-aged man had learned to do it to. He’d been chipping away at his trauma for his whole adult life. He’d learned that his trauma was way too much for any one person or situation, so he tried to release it a little bit at a time. He had learned to spread it out over a field of willing and trusted friends, like spreading manure over a pasture, or like Andy in the prison yard, one handful at a time, droppin right down his pant leg, the dust mixed in with the sweat and hairs on his leg.



Ever since he’d had his first conscious Presence experience, the Presence experience which was held by the form that was available. The young man embraced the Presence of G_d within the confines of the form that was available (the form of Christian fundamentalism). And this is the way of things as he understood them even now. He was embraced there in the form of his friend’s home. These two loving souls who were to receive this grateful man on that day. This healing man. This man who was determined to see. This man who wanted his children to live. No. Not just live. This man wanted his children to live a Life Abundant.



The young man and the woman had known that there was a problem, obviously. But they trusted that Jesus had taken care of it. She writhed and twisted during the worship services (the serpent rising from within?), the remnants of her trauma trying to surface. 



The young man had his own issues. He had recently been abandoned by his latest girlfriend, the one who was the buffer between him and his own random attraction to other males. He was unable to make peace with his own fluidity. He was scared (sacred) to death that his worst nightmare was coming true—or rather he was living his father’s worst nightmare.



He had a recurring dream. In the dream, he awoke, crawled out of bed, made his way to the bathroom mirror, and saw in his reflection a sleestack. Yes, a sleestack. A green humanoid lizard from the Saturday morning television drama of his childhood, The Land of the Lost. The meaning of the dream, or so he thought, was never difficult to see. He was a monster, the monster that his father was sure to warn him against. He was becoming the monster that could not be held—the monster that could not be known. The monster that would not be seen.



And it was in this way that the young couple emerged from their own deaths It was in this way that their consciousness continued its evolution. He had no context in which to understand himself that was deeper than the binary. And so it was within the confines of a binary fundamentalism that he found himself making peace with the authentic Life that was arising from within his own being. 



It was within the confines of this form that the couple tried to fit in. This is where they did the most natural thing in the world for a couple their age to do when they feel safe and warm and supported, they started a family. And it was good. It was the most love that either of them had ever experienced in their lives. And this form would continue to appear good for many years to come. It was this form, ultimately that the man and the woman would sacrafice their lives for, as every generation had ever done before them, sacraficing their own being so that these other beings might live. 



They just had no idea that they’d been born into a family of serpents. The impossible. The miracle.

I am not going to blame anyone. I am not going to blame you. I am going to bear all of this. I am going to own this, my friend. This has to stop here with me today. I will not pass this down to my children. I am not going to blame anyone.” 



There is no obligation to believe the story. It does not demand to be seen...ever. There is only an invitation to experience the story, an invitation to accept exactly what-is right now, to accept the All—to accept the current state of our evolution in the exact state that it is right now. That’s why the Christ spoke in parables, so that we could one day understand that the Christ is exactly that, a parable, a story that actually holds infinitely more space when it does not insist on being literal, when it demands no obedience, when it demands no respect. It’s a gentle process. It’s a patient process. There’s no hurry here. We’re just waking up. We’re yawning to a new dawn. Everything’s okay. Here we are. The nightmare is over. 4;30 AM



And so the writer found himself standing there in the great kitchen, facing North. His heels were hurting. “Where were we?” he questioned himself. “We were at Ron and Joann’s. That’s where we were.” He answered himself. 



“Yes. Ron and Joann’s,” the writer remembered now. 



The middle-aged man was held in the embrace of his friends love. He was held in the embrace of their home, that most sacred of forms as it was endowed by their beautiful Spirits. His friends, Ron and Joann held space for all of this to arise. They allowed the man to be. They had witnessed his journey for many years now. He had cried many times in their living room. Just as he had done many times before, he made peace with the refuge that was offered to him on that night. He accepted it just for what it was. Nothing less. Nothing more.



And it was in this way that the writer left Ron and Joann’s home that night. He returned to his own form, the gift that he had been given, these very words that we are sharing in right now, dear reader. These words around which we huddle as we seek refuge from the storms that rage within our own beings.



The writer’s thoracic back ached. He had not moved from behind the chromebook for a timeless moment. He watched all these writings happening before his eyes. He was not required to believe anything that he’d said. He was not required to start a new religion. He simply watched this miracle as the Christ was born again into this world through him. 



He wondered how he would feel right now if somehow this stream of consciousness were suddenly erased from existence. He wondered if another Naked Monk would ask him to do the impossible again. 



There are resolutions aren’t there, my Pema? (The man now confided with his great teacher Pema Chodron). Sentences do have periods, don’t they, my Pema. Paragraphs end, as do chapters in books and in lives. And books. Books have final pages, do they not, my wise Pema? 



“There are also bookends, good for holding us up when we there’s no shelf that will hold us,” his dear Pema responded with a smile. She continued. “Lives end. Entire species sometimes go extinct or evolve themselves to a new form, and therein lies the end of an era. The Universal lungs expand and contract, signaling the end of a cycle. There is also this cycle: The birth. The crucifixion (and the upside down cross, turning form on its head). The resurrection. The life cycle.” 



“Yes, Pema. I see,” said the middle-aged-man responded respectfully to his great teacher, The Universal Pema.



And it was in this way that the man found himself in dialogue with the Universal Wisdom. That which manifests itself in the echoing voices of our teachers. That voice that echoes from our teachers until their words are transcneded and integrated in to the ONE WISDOM that is in us all—That in us which only needs to be reminded of the truth that is already resounding in our bones.



Eli the cat crunched the food in his bowl which sat by the Universal water dispenser. Eli lapped the water from his red Universal water bowl. The Universal heater hummed as it warmed the home in which the Universal man found shelter. He lived by the kindness of his friend and AA sponsor, Dan G. This Universal man was on medical leave from his job. He currently had no income. He had just enough money to pay the next child support payment. 



The writer stood at the island in the kitchen of the great adobe house. He was facing West. He stepped away from the chromebook for a moment. He paused, leaning against the marble countertop. “It is my intention to give way where way is to be given,” he said. “It is my intention to let go, and let Life do the living.”





He did not have enough money to pay child support and also visit his mother for Christmas with his children, as planned. When his mother had asked him what he wanted for Christmas, he paused for several days before answering. “I just want to see you. Maybe some gas money so that I can come see you with the kids.” The middle-aged man had never known this way of life before. At least not in exactly this way. Not by himself.



He observed the barrier between himself and his audience. He remembered (was reminded) that in order for the reader to have her birth, he must disappear. It was his job to disappear, but he was not disappearing, in fact he was just then rising to the surface, nearly encountering the present tense. He toyed with this. 



He imagined it a smart and powerful literary feat that he’d accomplished. He knew that, although he was unaware of where and when this had been done, that it had already been approached, because the world is that big and time is that deep and this miracle of symbolic language was happening long before he was even conscious of these possibilities. Eileen’s words, “new genre” were causing their own little ego death, as they bounced around up there in his head. He then realized that that was part of their purpose.



The middle-aged man had been married to an English professor for nearly twenty years...maybe it was more than twenty years. Is it strange that he is now unable to recall? It seems like something that he should know. Anyway, because he had been married to an English Professor for many years, he was very familiar with that which he did not know. Or rather, he was vaguely aware of how muhch there was out there to be known.



He’d been to many English Department parties and befriended many incredibly gifted and talented thinker and writers, all philosophers of the English language. So, yes, the middl-aged-man had become well acquainted with that which he did not know. It was all out there, a beautiful mystery, and it was this mystery that he was now embracing with all the tutoring from the mother of his children and all those other professors from his past.



The middle-aged man was learning how to write, or rather he was being taught still by the mother of his children, the English teacher. There was a very physical aspect of writing that he found himself working with. Praise be to the laptop and its mobile nature. He was finding different places in the house to write. He now stood at the island in the kitchen, his chromebook propped with the two larger volumes of ACIM (A Course In Miracles).



Because of his wife, he was able to attended parties with people like Ed, the Marxist (whatever “Marxist” means), who had told him about the reified thunderhead (Ed the Mexican-American who could not help but joyfully make reference to reified-beans, assumedly our neighbors to the South). 



All this to say that he knew how terribly smart people could become, and he was quite familiar with his own intellectual limitations. He was just smart enough to really appreciate how smart someone else could be. He could watch it. He could observe it, just like some people watched him play music. However, some of the people he’d met, Like Ed, could play and philosophize, swimming in two realms, creating in that common space. Is this what was happening, was he becoming a Marxist?! Oh God, what would the writer’s mother think if he became a Marxist! “Have I caught the Marxist flu?” wondered the writer. 



And this is how the middle-aged-man worked in and around his beautiful ego which was playfully swimming around in his own being that morning.

# Day 3 December 21, 2019

Winter solstice

6:30AM



Those who see all creatures in themselves

And themselves in all creatures have no fear.

Upinashad

Darwin’s Prophecy:



Let the prophecy of Darwin be spoken forth. Let it be recieved. Let it be known that he was a prophet shining the light of salvation into this world. Let it be known that he suffered with the Christ in what he brought forth. Let it be known that he was fully human, fully tender and vulnerable in his efforts, and fully aware of the gravity that his message held. Let it be known that he brought forth his message with grace and dignity. 



Let it be known that science is a western Yoga. Let it be practiced. Let it be informed by Spirit. Let it inform the forms in which Spirit is practiced. Let it be known. 



The rational mind is not left behind as we transcend it. The age of reason, dear reader, was not a mistake. The scientific method is to be felt, and known and experienced. Let it be known that the practitioners of this yogic form are holy men, even if they themselves do not acknowledge that. It is another form of storytelling based in all matter which is all holy and compassionate and holds the story of unity within its very fabric. Matter is not separate from Spirit. All matter is the Christ. All is one. Praise be to all infinite matter!



This is the message that demands no attention. This is the message that forces no obedience. This is the message that is folded in on itself until the great contraction has ended this cycle.

It is only death that finally brings all form to its knees. And this death is holy and compassionate in and of itself. This death will come to those in lab coats. This death will come to those in monks robes. All are equal…but…there is depth. 



There is depth, dear reader. And this is what we are discovering here together. We are discovering how to acknowledge the depth, while not elevating ourselves above others (Thank you, brother Ken Wilber)





The Dying God

 

The old man waited patiently in the jungle clearing. White robes, flowing beard—a dying God—waiting for the man who had much to do with his imminent demise. Sounds of struggle emanated from the jungle brush just beyond the perimeter of the clearing. Using his staff, the old man lowered himself onto a large fallen tree. The disturbance in the underbrush grew nearer. 



Finally, a figure arose from the multitude of wide leaves. And there she stood, just having emerged from the bush. Se was a troubled woman in her mid-thirties—victorian skirts, disheveled hair wilted from humidity, face stained by dirt. She panted from her exertion. She stood there for a moment, relieved to be free from the forest from which she’d just stumbled. She scanned the clearing; her eyes met the old man’s. 



“My Lord?” she said, as she stumbled to stand before him.



“Yes, daughter,” He said.



She crumbled at his feet. Her eyes were now fixed on the patterns in her skirt. Tears began as silent, intermittent convulsions in her torso. Then, deep sobs arose from her chest. Her face contorted. Her eyes rose again to meet the old man’s gaze. Her mouth cracked open in tight expression of grief and thin strands of saliva stretched between her upper and lower lips. She remained there for quite some time. Her breathing steadied as her eyes met His. 



She raised herself slowly to her knees. Then she allowed her torso to collapse into the old man’s lap, hugging his abdomen. His hands naturally came to her head in an effort to comfort.

The two remained like this for a long moment as birds chattered and screeched in trees overhead.

 

“Emma?” said the old man, “Where is Charles?”



“He would not come,” she said. “His stomach is troubling him, and he is filled with anxiety at the thought of seeing you.”



“That is understandable,” said the dying God. “Emma, sit with me.”



Emma lifted herself from the old man’s lap and sat beside him now. She slumped, but she supported herself.



“All Gods must die Emma. It is how it has always been, and how it will always be. You know this to be true. I am merely the projection of what cannot be held in one form. I am only one projection of G_d, one image who points to that which is ALL that is real.”



Emma noticed that a small group of chimpanzees had gathered around them. An adolescent chimp approached the old man and jumped up in his lap. The old man looked thoughtfully into the primate’s eyes. The young chimp’s mother sat down in front of Emma, offering her curled hand. Emma could somehow sense the motherliness in this creature that seemed so horrifyingly familiar in form to herself—hands, eyes, feet, and breasts.



“I am the God of metaphor, Emma, the God of story. Just as all life has changed over time, so do our Stories. This form that you see now, this form that you practice, this lense through which you see life, must pass away to make room for a less…how should I say? A less fatherly figure? Less fatherly, Emma, but not to exclude the Father. The mother is rising Emma. The mother needs to be known if your species is to continue on its path of transmutation. I know that it is difficult for you to understand. I see that you are dying a death. I know that you are hurting. I see you, child. I see you. Let us rest there for a moment. Will you rest there for a moment with me? I see you Emma….Rest with me here for a moment. Let me hold you…



There is a long pause (a menopause)...Emma cries….Emma sobs...She begs for this to be taken from her...She knows this is more than she can hold...She is held by the spirit of this being that is passing into new form.

 

Being speaks…. “This death that you are dying is still the way of the cross, Emma. It is still the way that you have been shown. But, the way that you see me is changing. Your very perception of who I am is transmuting, if you will. This image is evolving, just as all forms have evolved before me. Novel forms are created from this process. You, my daughter are a novel form. You, my daughter, are being born again. Your species is being born again every moment. Without an understanding of this evolution, humanity cannot transcend the binary. Without this understanding the human species is trapped in the delusion of good and evil, trapped in a static prison. 

 

This evolutionary understanding is a result of the birth of the age of reason. Spiral dynamics. The serpent which spirals toward the infinite center of the sun and is drawn infinitely deeper and deeper into this consciousness. Your species is not static. Life is not static. Life is like a thundercloud changing, and ever changing. You must reckon yourself to this knowledge in order to experience the One-ness of all life. 



Your husband has discovered a key to unlocking the door to a much broader room, a more expansive field of consciousness. There will be those who take this message and turn it in to something that is not. There will be those who will say that Charles is a heretic. He will be mocked and hated by some for many many years to come, but this is the promise being fulfilled for those who choose to embrace the deepest callings. This is the very heresy that brings your species into a deeper communion with who I really AM. Just as Christ was a heretic, so are the ones who carry the light after him.



It is no different with you, Emma. You are carrying this. You have said yes to your husband and you have said yes to life. He has carried this as far as it will go. It is coming Emma. There is no stopping it. If it is not Charles, it will be someone else. The message of the prophet must amplify the One-ness in the ears of the people. The message of the true prophet recognizes all as ONE and the one as part of the ALL.

 

 

Those who see all creatures in themselves

And themselves in all creatures have no grief.

How can the multiplicity of life

Delude the one who sees its unity?

 

The Self is everywhere. Bright is the Self,

Indivisible, untouched by sin, wise

Immanent and transcendent. He it is

Who holds the cosmos together

Upanishad

# Day 3...8:56AM



The middle-aged man was, once again, standing at the marble island in the kitchen of the adobe house on the Eastern High Plains. Seventeen years ago, the sky was filled with red dust in this town where the man still lived and died. 



The man heard Dan G, his roomate making his way down the stairs. He was talking on his telephone by way of his headphones, dressed in his heavy, black jacket, kind of gliding along as he always seemed to do. Dan ended his conversation with his cousin, Dee. 



“Going for a walk?” said the middle-aged man. 



“Yes, sir.” said Dan.



“Well, I’ll go with you. Just let me get my jacket and some shoes.”



They got in Dan’s white Chevy Malibu and made the short drive to the track



They talked as they walked. The air was brisk. The golden grass on the infield of the track glimmered with frozen-white sparkling dew. The two men both proclaimed the walk a prayer for Dan’s health. Dan was concerned about his weight and the lack of physical activity in his life. The two friends reveled in one another’s company, as they always did when they had time together. 



Dan was now improvising quasi-Shakespeare-pentameter while the middle-aged man practiced his Irish accent, of which Dan was his teacher. They walked on the oval track for twenty minutes, renewing their friendship and proclaiming their undying love for one another. 



As they finished their walk. Dan collected a blue prayer flag from the track in remembrance of the prayer for health that they’d made together. They returned to the great adobe house in the Universal white Malibu. 



The middle-aged-man prepared oatmeal, as Dan NEVER cooked! They ate breakfast, trading inspiration, revelation, and much joy between themselves. They considered the hoi polloi. They watched building 7 fall again, that forgotten archive of New York City’s 9/11. They considered how the human species might suffer a death of the macro-ego. And finally, the Cliffs of Moher (More) where so many people had cast themselves into the sea to meet their own end. 



This was the usual gravity of their conversations. They were not men of shallow nature. Not today, at least. Not today, dear reader! Today they were alive and full of piss and vinegar! HaHa!



The middle aged man invited Dan to read Darwin’s prophecy. Dan read, then it was time for him to go. He had an appointment with his girlfriend. Before the two men parted each other’s company, they hugged one another as they recited the serenity prayer. This was their tradition. It had been some time since the middle-aged man had been to an AA meeting, it took him a moment to catch up with the prayer.



The writer returned to his work of writing in the Universal kitchen.



“Who is this?” Wondered the writer as he read the following poem. “It looks like Hafiz to me,” he responded to himself, “but we didn’t make a note of it, did we?” Forgive us, dear reader. We believe it to be Hafiz as translated by Ladinsky…with no title. Oh, please excuse us, dear reader.



We present to you, almost undoubtedly, our good friend, Hafiz!



Inside this new love, die.

Your way begins on the other side.

Become the sky.

Take an axe to the prison wall.

Escape.

Walk out like someone suddenly born into color.

Do it now.

You're covered with a thick cloud.

Slide out the side. Die,

and be quiet. Quietness is the surest sign

that you've died.

Your old life was a frantic running

from silence.

The speechless full moon 

comes out now.

The day progessed. The deaths and the resurrections continued. One moment passed away. Another moment was born. Peace was made. Wars were waged. People lived. People died. There is no accounting for the space of the rest of this day in the . It was not until later that evening that the man returned to his writing.
