# Day 7

11:18am



He faced north again

In the kitchen

His laptop perched upon

His bile (bible)

And all three volumes

Of the course in miracles

The cat scratched at the door

Eli

His friend

Who had checked in on him several times

Earlier that morning

As his body was trying to make peace with the lethal dose of medicine which he’d ingested earlier. His eyes were still dilated. His face still changed form in the mirror which he now faced. His face was the thunderhead. The man in the mirror looked tired. A little scared. He looked exhausted, actually. But, there he stood as Eli crunched his cat food. There he stood, the man who had lost his mind. The man who had lost his mind just earlier that morning. The man who decided to live. The man who had witnessed the texture of the light move from yellow to green. The man who knew that he was dying, or worse, that he would never be able to recover his mind, the medicine still showing him exactly what he needed to see, allowing him to experience exactly what he needed to experience. That he was not as ready to die as he thought he was.



Earlier that morning the man had risen from his kneeling position on the bathroom floor, his hair still dripping from the shower that he’d hoped would be his salvation. But, no. It didn’t quite do the trick. And he found himself desperately trying to make peace with exactly what he was experiencing. The man was gone. He was beyond recovery. And this is what he made peace with that time and time again, the fact that he was gone and he could not come back. As calmly as he could, he embraced the hopelessness of his situation as his mind turned over and again upon itself. 



He had witnessed the great folding in. Like blueberries in the muffin mixture that come in the can. His earthly mother had shown him how to rinse the blueberries in a colander so that they didn’t stain the whole lot purple. She showed him how to fold (not stir!) them into the mixture. They were folded over and over. 



The man had seen that this was how we are, like the blueberries in the mixture that his mother had so thoughtfully instructed him with. This is how we all make sense of our reality. We are folded into this mixture, turning over and over again, so that no one really has any control over any of it. We find ourselves meeting blueberries that we hadn’t seen for three or four or eight turns of the mothers rubber spatula. Yes. I was mothered. I was mothered. Thank God I was mothered by a woman who was trying to find herself. I was mothered by a woman who finally said, “That’s enough.”



And while her husband was gone away for some military training in Caifornia, she left. She checked in with her children, maybe even asked for their permission, which was freely given by the eldest son who was living life as if he was still in that shower being screamed at by the father. Was he still paralyzed in that shower? At any rate, he was full of a a lot of “fuck yous!” for his old man. 



The mother asked permission from her oldest son. Maybe she just wanted to know what he thought. Maybe she just wanted to know that he had seen what she had seen. Maybe she was just looking for a witness. Maybe she was reaching out to one of the only people in the world who she knew could understand what had just happened over the last 19 years. And what she found in her oldest son was as follows:



“Fuck him. Fuck that old man. Fuck that man who left me fearful in the shower. Fuck that mother-fucker who ripped the shower door off the hinges and screamed at me while I stood there paralyzed. Fuck him, Mom. You need to get the fuck out of here.”



And so it was that the mother left.



The nineteen year old Son stayed. The son stayed with the father. He did not go with the mother. The middle-aged-man does not remember if the invitation was given or not to go with his mother. The young man’s fifteen year old brother went to live with the mother in an apartment. But the nineteen year old boy-man stayed home with his father. The young man was there at the house. The young man was there at the house when the father came home. His father came home to a partially empty house, but the boy was still there. 



So the young man tried to make peace with his father, who arrived home to a very much empty home. 



“Did he try to make peace?” Aked the Great Mother? “Do you remember what was going on in that young man’s heart, son?”



“Mother?” said the middle-aged-man.



“Yes, Son?” said the, Great Mother.



“Will you help me to release this pain that is still in my heart? Will you help me release this trauma? Will you please take it from me?”



“Let me help you,” said the Great Mother.”



The young man with all the “fuck yous” in his heart, he stayed with his father. 



“Mother,” said the middle-aged-man, “Was he not ready to go? Was he afraid to go out into the world? Was he not ready to make it on his own? Why Mother, why did the young man stay, if he had all those fuck-yous in his heart?”



The man’s wife left him while he was away at military training. 



He was devastated.



The old man was devastated.



This writer cannot speak for what the old man went through after that. 

Just a snapshot that he shared once, a story which was relayed to the writer as something like this:



The old man stood, just inches away from a train. A lumbering train? A violent train? An inevitable train?



That’s the snap shot that the old-man shared with his son of his suicide meditation.



And so it came to pass that the old man blamed his eldest son, as if he had a knowing in his heart that the young man had empowered his woman to go.



And the old-man said to his son--in a fit of deep despair and instanity after he’d come home from military training to a partially empty house and the absence of his wife—The old man said to his son:



“You are the reason for this. This is all your fault. You are the reason she left me. You are the reason for my suffering, you little fuck.”



Praise be to the father. Praise be to this father. Praise be to the father who laid down his life so that his sons may live. Praise be to the father who was kicked and punched by his own father. Praise be to the father who wrestled with his own demons. Praise be to the father who tried. Praise be to the father who stood with his nose just inches away from the passing train. Praise be for the inevitable evolution that was taking place in him. Praise be to the father who was still a child. Praise be to this wounded one. Praise be to this hurting child. 



Please father, give him your praise. Give the praise to this son who never received the praise that a son deserves. Praise be to the grandfather, Vince. Vince, the one who only showed love and affection to this grandson. Praise be to all the pain that was carried throughout the generations. Praise be to the men who did their best to make peace with all of this. Praise be to the Great Turning. Praise be to the son’s heart which is turned toward the suffering father. Praise be to the impossible. Praise be. 



God

You must resurrect the old man’s life

For I cannot



“All I can do is meet him at Louie’s restraunt on Lake Hefner this coming Monday.

That’s all I can do father.

I will try to bring the grandchildren to see you

We will allow you to buy us lunch at Louie’s

It will be an honor

Thank you, Father

It will be an honor

I bless you father

With our presence

I say yes to you at Louie’s on lake hefner



The writer was facing North

Looking into the great mirror

Which was in the kitchen

In the adobe house

With the orange-pink floor tiles

Which the writer could still not remember the name of…the floor tiles

He knew they had a specific name

He could not remember that name



It was christmas

He had to pee again



It was 12:01



The writer’s consciousness shifts now, away from childhood, away from the distant past, as he recounts the events of his morning.



The bathtub where he’d lost his mind earlier that day was filthy…

Maybe there was a more gentle word than filthy…

Praise be to the medicine and the wisdom of the earth that resides within

“My purge is not filthy! It is sacred!” the middle-aged-man proclaimed.



And he wrote a song for the mushrooms, praising them for their act of turning the rocks into soil! All praise the fungus! He who helped make the earth what it is today!



The bathtub was littered with the excess medicine

That the dying man had purged

The purge that lingered in the water 

Around his skinny legs

The purge that he’d percolated in for a while 

The purge that slickened his skin



he rose from the cold tile

intent on living

after he’d seen the light change 

from yellow

to dull green

similar to the light change that he’d witnessed when the life had passed from the moth.



More praise be to the Owl Woman who had the middle-aged-man shelter for two nights at the loving cabin!

And more praise also to her mate, The Universal Stan, the one who brings us all together!



The man rose from the tile.

His mind was lost 

(This was nothing but really serious, you guys!

We can smile about it now,

But it was very serious then)

he searched for his pants



If he wanted to live

He knew

He must find his pants



“Forget the underwear!

I don’t need underwear to live,” he said

then he found his pants



his legs were slick from the great-percolating 

his legs were still slick with purge

he didn’t care

(well, he cared. But the purge on his leg was not too concerning in the light of the fact hat he had lost his mind, dear reader)

As he put on his pants he made his intention clear to G_d.

“I want to live, God! bring me back! I want to live! I’m not ready to go. It’s not my time!”



He had lost his mind. He was trying to live. He did not want to die. He had seen the edge. He had looked over. He was looking over the edge just then. Now he felt that he was way past his threshold; As a result he was rededicating himself to his intention to live. 



This man who just hours before, after taking the medicing, proclaimed to be ready to die the death. This very man was convinced that he was in a struggle to revive himself.



The man rededicated himself over and over and over again, praying that his father would bring him back from this death. The man had lost his mind, but he had not fully lost his composure. As he engaged himself in this process, it seemed to him that he had been training for this his whole life. He did not allow fear to have its way, even as he looked fear straight in the eye. 



He put his pants on. He found a shirt. He moved into the day, his mind still lost. He did not know how he would live with himself. He was afraid that his mind would not come back. He was in the great folding of the blueberries, he could not find his way out. He had ingested a lethal dose. Fear was there. Fear was right there. But, he did not do what fear said to do. He continued praying to his Father for restoration. 



He had lost his mind, but there was still hope. He was lost in the great turning-over. The light had signaled his demise. He knew that the might not make it back.



He had felt himself falling in to the changing of the light. But, he was unwilling to let go. 



He said, “No, this is as far as I am willing to go. I cannot go any further today.” 

And then he knew that it was time to call the ambulance to come and get him. He saw the ambulance arriving in his future. He saw himself at the ER. He saw himself back at the Sunrise Mental health facility, the place where he’d just been three-hundred-and-sixty-three short days ago. He knew it was time. It was the only way to save his life. He was dying or he had lost his mind. He felt that he may be forced to end his own life. He was unable to escape from the the great blueberry-batter-turning that he was experiencing. 



But, he accepted what-was. Over and over again he accepted what-was. Fear was speaking. Was fear speaking? The writer does not know now. Surely he could have given himself to fear. But, he did not. There was something deep inside the man that was very calm and knew just how to help the middle-aged-man. And this, dear reader, was a miracle (there are no large miracles. There are no small miracles. They are all of th equal value, and all flowing from the heart of love ACIM).



Over and over again, the man accepted what-was. The great What-Is. The man just kept agreeing with the great folding in that was happening in his being. He was at a threshold. He was at his peak. He wanted to come back home. He wanted to step away from this edge, but he could not. 



And so it was that the man came to find himself now wearing his favorite pair of pants but without underwear because underwear just never really occurred to him. It just wasn’t important. But, he knew that what needed to be done could not be done naked. Not today! He was grabbing for the fig leaf. He was looking for warmth. Praise be to those first beings who thought, “You know what, if we wear fur, we are not as cold. Let’s kill these great creatures, eat their flesh, and wear what they used to wear. Lets use their skin to keep our skin warm.” 



And so went history…the killing of other beings and the wearing of their skins



Selah



The man had pants on, but no underwear. He found a favorite shirt, a cozy longsleeve, textured and soft.



And so it went



The man who had lost his mind

he used all of his tools to find his way back

The man who had reached the threshold

The man who saw the light change from yellow

To a soft green

Just as it had when the moth passed



this was the man who decided to step back

the man who decided to live

the man who went as far as he knew to go 

the man who used the blender to dissolve the rest of the package of medicine

the man who drank it

the man who took it all in

He didn’t measure out the dosage

It was a lethal dosage

So much that his body knew that it must get rid of some of it

The man who had lost his mind



The middle-aged-man was still moving forward with his intent of living:



He was now walking toward the living room

That was where his oldest and most reliable tool was

His guitar

He began the song that had been coming in for weeks and weeks now

He began his song of surrender

He clinged to this form

the neck of the guitar felt foreign to him

but he knew that he could play

and so he did



He played as if his life depended on it

The man who had lost his life

The man who’d seen the light change from yellow

To a soft green.



He sang:

“I am humbled. I am broke.”

“I gave myself away by mirror and by smoke”

“Gospel man with feet of clay”

“I give myself away”

“I give myself away”



It was not the words that mattered

It was the form

The man was finding his way back into the form

The man was clinging to his song

Like a life raft

A raft of form

In a mind that was turning over and over again

A churning sea

The man was lost

His mind was gone

And he was reaching out to the form of this song

He knew he’d been practicing

He knew it could hold him



He prayed to his Father

He asked God to bring him back

He wanted to live

He had peered over the edge

He wanted to step away

He had lost his mind



And so it was that the man found himself, his guitar strapped over his shoulder, walking out into the cold christmas morning. He sang. He sang his song. He clung to the words. He clung to the form of it.



And so it was that the performance of a lifetime was given. He was aware of the presence of birds. He was aware of the tree Goddess, his sister with whom he had communed days before as the men were working just on the other side of those great evergreens. He sang. He felt the cold grass on his feet. He had not thought to put on any shoes. Or maybe the wisdom of the earth had made him unaware of that need so that his bare feet could touch the earth that day. His feet grew colder as he sang.



And so it went



He vamped on the chords and he sang out to God. He praised. He gave thanks and he asked God to bring him back from the edge. He asked God to restore his sanity. 



It was the performance of a lifetime. A non-performance…as he sang for his life to a living God. As he acknowledged the birds in song, he saw Ebenezer Scrooge running across the yard. He’d just woke up too! Ol’ scrooge made his way downtown to give his thanks.



He moved through the evergreen canopy. Hard blue seeds dotted the packed path.

He arrived in the meadow where he’d seen the faeries dancing just 2 days before. He wasn’t thinking about much of that, though. No. He was just singing for his life. Wondering if he could emerge from this with sanity.



As he arrived at the clearing He sang:



“if the ambulance is going to come

Let them come for a singing man”



“If the ambulance is coming

Theyre comin’ for a singin’ man”



It was the best song that he’d ever sung. The most fun song. The funniest song of determination that he’d ever composed. The songwriter was accepting of his fate, but if it was all over then he was ready to go out singing!



“I give myself away”

“I give myself away,” he sang over and over again.



The sun was just rising between the tallest eversgreens. He could feel its warmth. He praised the sun for its warmth.



Over and over again. The vamp continued. Two chords back and forth. Abolutely no thought at all needed in the strumming. In the playing. He had been practicing for this moment all of his life. The moment when he would sing his self back home. He sang, waiting for the medicine to work it’s way through. He had taken a lethal dose. He had lost his mind. 



Then he saw that there was a chance that he could live.



He turned and faced the evergreens to the West. He sang to them. He praised them for their wisdom. “I want to know who you are,” sang the man. “I need to know you. Please show me how to be with you. I love you. How do you live? How do you live such rooted lives? I praise the soil from which you arose! Please sisters, show me how to rise up from the earth. Show me how to live.”



And so he sang to the trees in this manner

And so he sang to the birds

And so he sang to the sky



The non-performance of a lifetime



And so he sang to the ONE 

And so he sang to the Father

And so he sang to the Mother

His sisters

And his brothers

In this world



And his feet were no longer cold

They were numb

Comfortably numb

Beautifully numb and one with the earth



And so it happened that he saw the grass

He saw again for the first time how beautiful the golden grass could be in the winter if it hadn’t been subjected to a final cut

He saw how the grass had grown tall in places

And he saw it holding form



This was the field…again

This was the field that he’d sold everything for

This was the field that, as a young man, he’d sold all he had 

Once again, he saw his field

And he knew the treasure that was hidden in his field



And so it came to pass that the man’s mind was being restored.

But it was not restored yet



The feeling in his feet came back

His feet were very cold now



He was finally able to recall the last verse

Or, perhaps, the last verse was restored to him



And so he sang:



God is hot and God is cold

I felt his angel 

Give me meek

And give me bold

Naked is the way I came

That’s how I give myself away

I give myself away



The man completed the circle around the property. He longed for the warmth of the great adobe home now. 



He opened the back door, walked over the threshold, and closed the door, just as the fathers who invented the door had planned. “Oh, lets make a barrier that we can open and shut at will, choosing as to when we allow things in and out,” thought the fathers who had created the door. Praise be to the fathers who created the doors that keep out the wild beasts and the wind!



And so it went that the man placed his guitar on the kitchen table and began to engage himself with the things of the kitchen. He continued to sing. His mind was still in the process of coming back to him.



He sang



If the ambulance is coming

She’s comin’ to a home 

Where the dishwaher

Is runnin’



And so it was that he rinsed all the silverware and plates and placed them in the diswasher. He cleaned the skillets, giving praise to God for another dirty dish. “Thank you father for this dirty skillet. Thank you for this pie pan!”



And so it was that he washed and dried a wooden handled spatula, which his mother had instructed him should never go through the dishwasher.



So it was that he saved a wooden handled spatula from that terrible fate on that day. And he washed the spatula by hand. And he dried it profusely as he sang:



If the ambulance is comin’

Theyr’e comin’ to a home 

Where this spatula is right here in its proper place



And so the spatuala was placed exactly where it needed to be in case of the ambulance’s arrival.



And so it went that the man cleaned the kitchen enthusiastically, but not perfectly by any means. It was far far from a perfect cleaning. Very very far from a perfect cleaning, but the cleaning that was done was done with his whole heart, every remaining morsel of food on the dishes acknowledged. He threw plastic cups away that should have been reused. That was okay. Perfection was not necessary. He was here, in the kitchen, participating in this form. He was not ready to die. He had not been able to let himself die. He needed a guide to die that death. He needed a shaman. He needed community to help him make that journey into the dull green light. He had gone as far as he could by himself. He would need help to go that deep again.



And so it came to pass that the man, having come from the fields singing, cleaned his kitchen…Cleaned Dan’s kitchen…the kitchen in which the writer so graciously wrote. He faced into the large mirror, the medicine still present with the writer. He started writing.



So it came to pass that the author died that day

Or he learned that he was not ready to die

he had some kind of lesson in death

A lesson in what it was to lose one’s mind



A lesson in what it was like to come back to form

After being folded over and over again

In the vast evolving consciousness.



He remembered Kyle Seitsinger

And the boys…the men who died over there

Wherever “over there” was



He acknowledged his own pain

He acknowledged the tenderness of this process

and the gift that he was experiencing in the working out 

Of all this



He brought his hands together,

Placed the back side of his thumbs to his forehead

and bowed his head toward his chest

The dying author

Bringing life to His audience



Praise be to God!

The great What IS

The great I AM

The ONE who restores our minds

Our bodies

Our souls



To wholeness



Amen

Selah

# Day 8

1:34AM



The dying author awoke at 1:34AM, the day after Christmas. The day after he ground up what he estimated to be 10 grams of dry mushrooms and drank it all at once. He questioned the wisdom of that. He wondered if he had done some kind of violence to himself. The journey of yesterday morning had been the single most scary experience of his life.



He realized that he was going to need help to continue this healing journey. He did not know from where or how that help would come.



The middle-aged-man had a trip planned. It was Thursday. Tomorrow he would go with his three children and his son-in-law to Oklahoma City. He was running out of money. This morning he felt as if he was running out of patience with himself. He felt foolish for putting himself through what he had yesterday with the medicine. 



At the time, he felt that he was being shown to eat all the mushrooms, but now he was not sure. He had made himself sick, and been unable to allow himself to sink in. He had to save his own life. He was unable to surrender. He felt that he had done violence to himself in taking in the medicine the way he did. He needed help.



He walked away from his job

He had no income

His bank account was dwindling

His ex wife would be expecting a child-support check

He did not have the money



He prayed the simplest prayer

The one that he had seen work

“God, please help me.”



Eli came and cuddled in close to the mans chest, purring in undulating waves.

The man massaged his head and felt the purring in his chest.



“God, please help me.”

Please send me the help that I need

How can I make peace with a universe that is out to help me?

Can I accept that right now?

That the universe is out to help me?



The middle aged man was tired. He was tired of working for food that only left him hungry. He was tired of trading his life for dollars. He wanted something else. No. He needed something else. His being was crying out for something else. He felt that he was at the end of a long journey. He felt that he was at the beginning of a longer one. “How can I help?” asked the man. “how can I help in this great turning?” “I have made myself available. Have I made myself available? How can I help?”





The man recalled one brief moment of his trip yesterday, lying in bed. He was a baby, struggling for attention. Struggling to find the nipple. His thumb became what he sought. He cried out for attention. He cried out, in this infant state, for the help that he needed to survive. A child is born.



The writer longed to live at the speed of life. To allow his life to unfold, not by the schedule of a physical therapy clinic, where he was bound to heal when his schedule called for healing. He had learned over the last eight years, working in the medical system just how impossible that was for him. 



The only way that he knew to be with these hurting people was to give them his whole heart. To give them the full attention that they deserved. To be fully present. But the man found that when he did this, when he participated in the healing process in this full measure, he became hopelessly depleted, exhausted, no longer able to function, unable to give these hurting people what they needed. 



A weekend was not enough recovery time. A week was not enough recovery time either . His job expected him to be available for forty hours a week , 50 weeks a year. The man had given his everything to make it work for himself, but he could not.



He came back time and time again after being depleted and breaking down. He had gone as far as he could go, and one day, as he sat in prayer and meditation in the bathroom, as he sat in the exact place that this writing project began, something crystallized in his being. He was ready for something else. He was ready to give himself the chance that he needed. He was finally ready to walk away from all his dysfunction. 



Something came together right before him. It was not a particularly emotional moment. It was a simple moment in which he knew what needed to be done. So he went to work and typed his two weeks notice. He wanted to honor his patients and his boss and his coworkers by completing the two weeks notice, but he could not. He was unable. He had literally come as far as he could go. He was not quitting because he wanted to. He was quitting because he had to. He was quitting because he was no longer able to fit his true Self into this round hole. He was finished. It was not a sign of illness, it was a sign of health.



And this is how the writer found himself that morning after having eaten the mushrooms on the day after Christmas. The writer lay in bed, his laptop propped up on the tiger blanket that his youngest daughter brought to him from home after he had walked away. 



For twenty months now, the man had been stepping away. He stepped away from a twenty year marriage. He stepped away from a passionate love affair. He stepped away from a friends-with-benefits relationship. He stepped away from his job. He stepped away from the community of a 12 step program so that he try to give himself the healing that he needed through psychedelics. And now, he was trying to step away from the ego that was stifling him. He was trying to step away from the programmed ego. The self that had been programmed by a dysfunctional society. The false-self that had grown up around him for protections. The self that protected itself at all cost. The self that does not trust that there is enough. The self that is critical. The self that is wounded. The self who is scared. The self who is ashamed. The self who is resentful. The self that cannot let go.



The middle-aged-man wanted to move at the speed of life. He wanted to be alert when he was awake. He wanted to sleep when he was tired. He wanted to allow inspiration to come and go. He wanted to heal when the Father was healing and rest when the Father was resting. He wanted to allow himself to live. He wanted to allow this true Self to arise from within.



“Mother?” said the middle aged man. Can you shine your light on all these “wants?”



“Yes, my son,” My light is shining.” She smiled.



The author scanned through some of his work from the last days, but he was unable to feel anything but demoralized. He remembered Eilleen’s words from the email she’d sent, about how his self-compassion would be important during these down moments. The middle-aged-man allowed himself this weariness. 



He allowed himself this moment. He flipped his laptop closed. He lay there in his bed. He Curled the tiger blanket around his body. He stuck his thumb in his mouth, trying to recall the baby that he’d become the day before after he’d consumed all that medicine.



“Please, hold me,” he said, in a pitiful voice. “Please, hold me. I just want to be held.”



Over and over again, “Please hold me. Please hold me. Please hold me.”



He lay there wishing that he would have been able to sink into the death that was offered him, that death that was offered by the mushrooms (Praise be to the wise ones!), the death that he’d been offered when the light turned from yellow to dull green. He wished that he could have seen what lie beyond that threshold, but instead he had prayed to live. Instead he had gotten up, put on the fig leaf, grabbed his tools and saved himself. 



He allowed himself to sink into that death now. In his mind, he went back to that moment there on the bathroom floor when his hair was dripping wet. He released all his ambition. He had no job. He had no future. He had no desire. No desire to continue this writing project. No desire to ever return to work. He had no desire to travel to Oklahoma City with his children to see his mother. He wanted to just sink back into the earth.



Eli, curled up beside the dying man. He was quite still for a few moments. Then, Eli made a very subtle movement, a movement which registered in the man’s senses with profundity. The middle-aged-man found himself there, present with Eli. He found himself present again with the simplicity of Eli’s next subtle movement. 



He sensed in this moment, present here with another living being, a great joy, a simple presence. He observed himself sensing Eli. He was delivered from his own pity for a moment. He was no longer the narrator. He was in a simple state of being. Then, just as quickly, he was back again. The voice of the narrator returned. The voice of the writer. “Ahhhh, thought the writer, this is what I’ve been waiting for, I’ve been writing about you, my friend.” He acknowledged the simple presence of being. The writer was acknowledging the Great I AM. The writer then acknowledged that one with which he was so familiar, that one who tells stories, his beloved muse, that individual. He made peace with that voice, and then he was allowed to sink back into the death, or the life beyond the death. Then, again, the writer disappeared. The man, having some simpler I AM state of being. The man experienced the God who was his own experience. He experienced the theosis. The one-ness. 



The middle-aged-man had felt that writer’s voice developing in him over the last eight days. Over the last eight days of intensive writing, the voice of the narrator had become strengthened and fortified, reinforced. The voice was so strong now that it had begun to speak within the man’s being, even when he was not in front of his laptop facing North. The voice had become so distinct from his being that the man recognized it for what it was, the storyteller. Who is the storyteller? The one who speaks in parables? Who is that one? The one who tells no story of himself? The one who writes no book? The one who lives with absolute presence? The one who does not speak of himself, but who speaks of The One-ness? Does this one live in me?



The middle-aged-man, still lying in bed, turns once again to his inner being. He lay there with Eli. He phased in and out of being-states. When the storytell told a story, he acknowledged that one. Sometimes the story teller became silent, or he allowed the storyteller to take a much deserved rest. Yes, the man allowed his storyteller to rest. 



The storyteller, the one who tells the story of hopelessness. The one who tells the story of the bank account. The one who tells the story of the individual. The one who grew up hurting, just dying to be heard. The one who is desperate for attention. The baby that never got the love that he wanted or needed. The one who was angry and crushed. The one who came forth into the world. The one who was chased around the tree by his father on the day that he left home. The one who was still suffering. The one who failed in the workplace. The one who failed in his marriage. The father who failed to give his own children everything they needed. The one who was responsible for the repossession of his two youngest children’s cars. The one who would one day be homeless, like Jedi 9. The one who could not allow himeself to sink into the dull green light. The one who had to defend himself.



Praise be to Pema, who introduced the man to the practice of vipassana. Praise be to Penny for introducing him to Pema. Penny, the one who had introduced him to “unconditional positive regard. Praise be to Carl Rogers, the father of unconditional-positive-regard in psychotherapy. Praise be to the Source, from which all unconditional positive regard flows. Praise be to the great I AM. Praise to the great Being from which we all flow and will return. Praise be to the promise of the dull green light. Praise be to the one who speaks of the kingdom of heaven in parables. Praise be to the One who says “yes” to the dying process over and over again even as he is sowing his own life back into the soil. Praise be to the author who, for even a brief moment descends to a deeper state of being and communes with the great I AM. Praise be that there is more than what we can see. Praise be to the great Mystery, that which cannot be spoken of. Praise be to Bruce, and all those who keep speaking of that which is beyond all language. Praise be to the fingers curled over home row. Praise be to the great What-Is. Praise be to Bill W and Dr Bob for crystallizing the twelve steps for all of those who would hear, for those of us whose lives had become unmanageable. Praise to the father who suffers, yet does what he can to shelter and love his children. Praise be to the failure, which is really no failure at all, just a natural expression of the evolution of deeper consciousness. Gratefulness flows from within no. May gratefulness overflow from deep within our beings. May we be overwhelmed by life. May we be overwhelmed and consumed by the great Snake which spirals into the infinite universe of material and consciousness. May we see the Christ in all and the All in Christ. May we praise the Christ in all that we see. May we live lives of merry abandon to the Oneness. May we embrace our individuality with unconditional positive regard. May we notice the subtle movements of the great cat, the Lion of Judah. May we acknowledge and accept every gift that life has to offer. May we follow that life to the end, when the dull green light invites us back into the great Presence.



The man’s prayer changed, as he lay there on his side, Eli next to him. “God,” he said, “help me to see how you are holding me. I know that I am being held. Please help me to experience your embrace. I know that you are holding me. I am finished God. I am at the end. I cannot go on if I do not know your embrace.” The man remained in that space for some time. Then something came to him.



As he opened his laptop, a song came to the middle-aged-man. He lay in bed, typing in a reclined position. his Chomebook was propped up on the tiger blanket which his daughter had so lovingly delivered to him just after he had left home twenty months ago. The song went like this



Oh Lord, I long to know your embrace

Oh my soul longs sorely after you, Oh my God

Oh Lord I love you so

I have nowhere else to go

Before the cock crows

I know

I will say, 

“no, I do not know you.”



In the past months the man had come to relate to the story of Peter in a very personal way. Peter, the Rock, this man who was a witness to the life of Christ. The man who knew this Lord, his lover. This man whom he had fallen deeply in love with. Peter, the one who dropped his nets to follow this man who he was deeply attracted to, because…That’s how the story goes, right?



There was a human that walked the earth who was so attractive to other men that they left their homes and their wives to be with him. And all these men sat together at night and shared deep passion with one antother. They were having a very personal experience together. It was a taboo experience. An intimate experience. All these men had left everything to follow this man that they called, Lord. 



These men were falling in love, and the love that they were making with each other, the power of this One and these twelve coming together, was the seed which was impregnating the world with the Christ. This taboo love affair that these men were having with one another was going to make us pregnant with the spirit of Christ so that his consciousness could be born again. That’s how hard these men were fucking the earth and its inhabitants. It was very passionate!



And after this One and these twelve men had made love to the world like this, and it was time for the Christ to do the impossible, when all the shit was coming down, when those who were in charge finally said, “That is ENOUGH! We won’t stand for this anymore. We won’t stand for these men roaming about making love to the world anymore. This is a huge fucking problem and it is threatening everything that we know! We must put a stop tot this!”



And so it was determined that the guards would go and get this ONE. This one from which all this love making had originated. And they came, and there was Peter who tried to protect him, because he loved him so. And an ear was cut off with a sword. And the Christ, in that moment said, “No, this is not how it goes.” And he replaced the ear that had been cut off (Van gogh’s ear?). The ONE miraculously replaced the ear, then went with the guards.



This ONE who had been taken away by the guards, He was the only one who understood what it was that was about to happen. Earlier, he’d had a conversation with Peter. Peter said to the ONE, he say, “I love you so much, my friend, my lover, my Lord. I will never forsake you. I will never turn away from you. I see you, my Lord. You are the most beautiful being that I have ever known. I would not walk away from you. Please, hold me, tell me everything is going to be okay.” 



“Peter,” said the Christ, “I know that you love me, and I love you. It has been a deep honor to spend this time with you. It is true that we have been together for quite some time. We have seen so much. We have miracles happen by the love in our hearts. I would love to stay with you. I would love to live more life with you, but I must go do something else. I have to show you something. I have to work this one last miracle. I have to go and do the un-do-able. I have to do something that will offend you. It will sicken you so deeply. What is going to happen is going to scare you so deeply. You will be so afraid for your own life that you will tell everyone that you do not even know me, Peter. What is going to happen is going to invoke such a great fear in you that you will run. You’re going to run Peter. You’re going to rise up and do whatever it takes to save your own life, because that’s just how much gravity that this situation holds (gravity? There was no gravity back then.). 



Anyway Peter, this is how it’s going to go. I know you love me. But you are approaching your own death tonight. You’ve been brought to the threshold. I will pass through my doorway and you will pass through yours. This threshold that I am about to cross, I am the only one of us who can make that trip. I’ve been training all my life for this, Peter. I have the necessary tools. I have this deep abiding relationship with my Father. I don’t quite understand it all Peter, but this is just who I am. This is how I have always been. It has been an honor to travel with you Petra. It has been an honor to hold you, to touch you, to smell you, to laugh with you. It has been an honor to make this love with you. 



Don’t be disheartened, Petra, when you betray me, for this is just the way of things. This is just how it goes. Petra, you’re not just going to betray me once. Not twice. But three times. Before the rooster crows, Petra, my rock. You will say that you don’t know me three times, my friend. And then you will die a death my Petra. Your heart will break as you watch me suffer, and there will be absolutely nothing that you can do about it. Now hug me, one last time. Let me hold you one last time before this all happens, my Petra. Oh God, I love you.”



And how was Peter feeling after that embrace? What was in his heart? How was he holding all of this? How was he held? I don’t think that we have to even open our bible to know. He was struggling. The One that he loved had just spoken over him a prophesy of failure? Is that what had happened? Maybe. Or maybe the One had just given him the message of “unconditional positive regard”. 



Because here’s the thing: Those two men held each other in that embrace for quite a long moment that afternoon. They cried in each others arms. And as the Christ said these next words to him, Peter felt a love flow into his being that he would remember again only after he had betrayed his Lord three times. Because of the great fear that came over this strong man, He forgot all about this exchange. The next time that Peter would even remember this impartation of love was just after the cock crowed that next morning, because fear completely overtook the man. And this is what the Christ said to Peter during that hug that was way too long for a couple of straight guys:



“There is nothing that you can do, My Petra, that will make me stop loving you. I know that you are human. I know that you are scared. I understand your limitations. But you will find your way back to the love that we made here. Your whole life is changed forever because of the love that we have made here, and now your DNA has been changed. You very being is forever altered by this miracle that has been done through us. You will spend the rest of your life trying to understand what you have seen here. You will spend the rest of your life in remembrance of these miracles, bearing witness to the light that has passed through you during this time. And you will live and you will die, but this message is going to keep speaking for generations and generations to come. Two thousand years from now, they’re still going to be grappling with this. They’re going to do a bunch of crazy shit with our story, Petra. Our love will be betrayed time and time again, by men who think they know, by those who are full of fear. But the point is, Petra, that I am always holding you. The Anointed one is always with you now, and it has nothing to do with you how good you are. You know that the love I have given you is unconitional. The love of the Father always finds his Sons. Allow yourself, Petr to be held by this absolute acceptance. Be held in this perfect love that we hae made together. Share this love that we have made. Make this happen again. Allow yourself to be held by this absolute grace, My petra. I’ll be back soon. There’s more I can share with you then, my friend. Peace to you. Now, Go on, orphan, read some books!” (nacho Libre? Yes or no?)”



This is my story

This is my song

Loving my savior

All the day long



La la la la la

La la la la

# Day 8

Dec 26 2019

7:38 AM



The man recalled a moment when he was younger. It was a moment that occurred some time after he’d sold all he had so that he could buy that field—that field where he’d reburied the treasure that he’d found. 



After he and his wife had sold all they had--after they had bought that field, the voice of the Lord seemed to go silent. Everything that the young man had learned, all of his spiritual practice was beginning to break down. 



The young man was learning to live in this world with a young family. He was reconciling himself to the needs of his family, to the needs of his wife. He was in the process of giving himself away. He was the seed that was being sown into the soil. He was the dying seed from which the tree would grow. He was being folded in to the blueberry batter. He was discovering what all this was like.



This young man—this still traumatized young man--was working at Braums, a popular chain of fast-food restaurants in Oklahoma. The young man was a soda jerk. He made and served ice-cream and hamburgers. The first time he had placed his hand under the heat lamp to retrieve some salty fries from the warmer he cringed. 



The writer recalled the heat of the red lamp on his skin. He recalled the first time that he was forced to ask the question, “Do you want fries with that.” He recalled the washing of the dishes and the mopping of the floors. He recalled how he would crawl inside the trash can container (the one with the swinging door that says “thank you” as you place your trash as you leave the restaurant). 



He crawled inside the trash can receptacle to clean the dried ketchup that had slopped in there. It was the most honest expression that he could find, crawling inside the trash can. He had not seen anyone else do it, it was just his intuition that lead him in there. He felt safe inside the trashcan receptacle, cleaning the dried ketchup. It felt honest in there. 



“Did it feel honest, my Son?” asked the mother? Or did it feel safe in that trashcan?”



When the young man was in the trash can he felt that no one would question his willingness. He sat in there with the dried ketchup. It was a moment of surrender. He surrendered to the lowest possible task, the one that he knew no one would question. No one would question his willingess or his commitment when he was in the trash can. He was safe in the trash can receptacle, scraping the dried ketchup off the walls.



And so it went that the young man continued making peace with this world, working for minimum wage at the Braums, Ice Cream and Dairy Store. He got the job at Braums immediately after he had sold all that he had to buy the field, just as he and his family were moving in with a woman from their church. A strong woman named Maryanne. A spirit filled woman. A woman who said yes to the prophets who asked to come live with her. These two brave young souls had just sold all they had in order to buy that field. The final thing that this young couple sold was their white Pontiac. The same Pontiac that had been given to them by the mans father-in-law, the one who’d warned him about the devil’s cock and semen. The one who was right in his discernment. 



The white Pontiac, a gift from the father in law to the family, was the last item they sold. This was the final possession that they sold. The Braums, however, was over a mile from Maryanne’s home. Sometimes the young man had to walk when Maryanne could not give him a ride. 



“BLESSYA” was how the license plate on Maryanne’s gold Honda read. Maryanne, this woman who took the young family into their home. Maryanne, this woman with an entire bookshelf wall filled with spirit-filled Christian books. Maryanne, this woman who had given herself to the Spirit. This woman who had given herself to the saying of “yes” to the Spirit of the Lord.



And so it came to pass that the young family lived with Maryanne.



The young family lived with Maryanne for God knows how long. There really is no telling, dear reader. The wife may still remember, but dear reader, it does not seem a good time to reach out to her right now, as she seems to be uninterested in any friendship.



The young family were given two rooms. They all got along quite well it seems, to a point. The difficulty began with a deliverance session. 



The man and the woman were interested in sanctification. They wanted all of what God had for their lives. The writer does not remember the exact circumstances under which he and his wife submitted themselves to an exorcism on that evening, as they took turns holding their baby daughter while the other was alone in a room with the two women who had the authority to cast out all types of demons.



The writer does believe that it was during this time that Maryanne discerned that the young wife probably had not truly given her life to the living Christ. This came with some shock as she shared the news with the young husband. He’d never considered this possibility. Maryanne was a mentor of his. She was showing him in the ways of the Spirit. Yes, it was all very confusing to him really.



The young man, this one who was in the process of exploring fundamentalism to it’s insane ende, was more confused than he was capable of understanding. For it was the trauma that those women had tried to cast out of these two young parents that night. Each of these young ones had endured crippling trauma in their childhood. There was not enough help. There was not enough holding. There was not enough understanding within the bounds of fundamentalist christianity for the type of deliverance that these two lovely young people needed.



The couple both understood that it was time for them to leave Maryanne’s house. The young man was stretched between these two women—his wife the one he was trying to love with all of his heart, and his spiritual mentor who had informed him that she was in need of salvation. Dear reader, I think you can see how this was confusion for a young man raised in a dysfunctional home and very little in the way of effective people skills.



And so it came to pass that the young family qualified for a HUD loan and were able to buy their first house. And it was a little red brick house which stood directly in the shadow of a light blue water tower. Maryanne loaned them the money for the red dodge Caravan that would eventually burn up at mile marker 428, just outside the little college-cow-town. 



After the young family was reestablished in a home of their own, the young man was promoted to shift manager and he was given a position at the busiest Braum’s store in the state of Oklahoma, located at the intersection of 122nd and MacArthur. The young man arrived at this store with a very short haircut. You see, dear reader, he wanted more than anything to become a police officer. 



He was trying desperately to make some sense of his life. There was a story that he was trying to tell about himself. The story was of a powerful young man who once was lost and now he was found. A man who used to smoke pot and play music, but who turned his life around and became an upstanding member of his society. 



He was ready to join. This young man who had an emotional breakdown at Army basic training, this young artist, he was still cutting his hair short and trying to join something. He wanted to be held. He wanted so deeply to be held by the system, by the kin-dom that was all around him. 



God was no longer speaking to him in the way that He had in the beginning of his salvation experience, and now he felt that all that was left to do was find a way to be. He was constructing his life’s container. He was saying “yes” to the form that was. And it looked like it would be great fun to carry a gun and talk softly and calmly into a radio. He imagined himself finding the same respect that the officers had at his church.



The man’s wife dropped him off at Braums that day. She drove him to work so that she could have the car to trun errands. The young man who was sitting in that car that day did not want to go to work at Braums. He wanted to be a police officer. He was becoming depleted. His job made him feel terrible about himself. The angry customers were more than the could bear.



Dread filled the young man’s heart as he made his way through the parking lot. He pushed open the double doors. The dread of inevitable failure awaited him within these walls. Although he worked at the busiest store in the state, upper management did not allow enough workers to truly cover the volume of sales that the store did every day. There were always disgruntled customers and long lines. There was nothing the young man could do to prevent this from happening. 



He ran around as fast as he could, the shift manager, trying to serve as best he could, sometimes speaking Spanish to his fellow Mexican employees. This made him feel kind and open to the world. Speaking Spanish to his fellow employees made him feel as if he was growing, or travelling, or learning, or respecting others in a way that he had never before. Even when he made a fool of himself in the speaking of the foreign language, he felt good about himself and his effort.



On the evening shift, customers rarely stopped pouring in the doors. “Oh, they look so miserable waiting in line,” the young man thought. “Oh, these people are so angry. I can hardly stand angry people,” said the young man’s traumatized little boy who was imprisoned in fear deep in the man’s chest. “They get so angry when their order is not right. There’s just nothing I can do about this. This is too much! We can’t handle it here! It’s not safe here! We’ve got to get out of here,” cried the scared little boy. 



This was how it came to pass that one day, after struggling with this situation for weeks, the young man found himself unable to move. He stood there by the ice cream freezer at the entrance to the work area. He imagined that the stickiness from the ice cream on his shoes was preventing him from taking the next step. But he knew that it was not the ice cream that was preventing him from moving. It was something else. What prevented him from moving was something inside him. He could not tell if he was unable to move, or if he was just unwilling to move. There was something inside of him that was unwilling to move. It was the same something that he had forced himself past many many times in the months that he had been working at Braums. It was an unwillingness that he knew how to override, but in this moment, the unwillingess seemed to be speaking to him so calmly, so quietly, in such a voice that he knew he would not pick up his sticky feet to scoop another double dip from the freezer.



“Were you there with me, Mother?” questioned the middle-aged-man, “What is it that I need to see here? Please shine your light on my insides. How do I take the next step, Great Mother? This is so much bigger than I am. I’ve walked away so many times. I’ve picked myself up so many times. I am tired mother. As I look at the suffering of this young man I realize the immensity of it all. I am deeply humbled by life. I am scared sometimes that I am just not enough for all of this. Can you see my insecurity Mother? Can you see how I am hurting? Can you see my tenderness? Are you going to tell me what is wrong with me Mother? How will I recover? How will I live. I sit here typing, Mother. I sit here, hoping that you are continuing to open my heart. Shine your light, dear Mother. Please illuminate my heart.”



And so it came to pass that the young man did pick up his feet, but it was only to take a step backward to where his manager was sitting at a booth. He was working on the schedule for the upcoming week. 



“How can I help you?” the manager asked, as the young man presented himself.



“I’m done,” said the young man, “I can’t work here anymore.



The young man informed his manager that he was done, that he could not work another minute and he walked out the door without a job. His wife and child arrived in the red mini-van to pick him up, this young man who had just quit his job because it was too overwhelming. He didn’t have the heart for that. 



Many jobs came and went after that. He worked in construction, the second man on a two man crew run by a white-haired Vietnam veteran who treated him well, Tom Neeley was his name. 



At guitar center, he hid in the acoustic room, seeking refuge from the chaos in the main sales floor. All those flashy guitar licks and chum-chumming out in the main room was overwhelming for the young man. Do you know what was also overwhelming to the young man? The pressure to sell. He was not a closer. He liked to show people guitars, but he was definitely no salesman.



He eventually realized his dream and became a police officer, where he was shown the injustice that the justice system heaps on those who it was created to serve. After leaving the police force, he was depressed and resentful. He made music until the family’s money ran out. That’s when the family found themselves moving to New Mexico.



With the help of his wife’s aunt and uncle they were hired at a Children’s home in New Mexico. The young man hoped he would discover “true religion” there. The bible said that it was true religion to serve “orphans”. He was still looking for a form that could hold him. He needed to be held. 



The young man, however, did not feel held at the Children’s Home (This is no surprise to you now, dear reader). 



It was then that his music was revived in him. A door was opened to the young man. A door that filled him with hope and joy. Over the net years, he was hired to teach guitar and bass at a number of learning institutions. He was given an office in the music building at the local University. His name became known in his small town. The young man was able to feel more self-respect than he ever had experienced in his whole life.



The young man eventually learned to teach with compassion. He practiced and taught his scales and arpeggios. He continued writing songs. He performed, hoping for more respect. He worked as hard as he knew, trying to emulate his incrediby hard working wife. He often felt a part of thins. But he needed to be heard more. He needed to be seen. He longed to be held, often wanting the Spirit of Music to do for him what the Spirit was apparently not willing to do. 



The Young man produced an album. The young man risked everything to get on the road and promote the album. The young man waited for the recognition to come that he knew that he deserved. He played for appreciative audiences. He had mountain-top performance experiences, but it was never enough. 



He noticed that the day after these mountain-top experiences were the worst days of his life. The emotions that he allowed himself to experience during his performance, the attention that he got in those brief moments. He just wanted more. He never wanted to get down off the stage. “Why don’t the people of this world want me to sing for them every day? Wondered the young man. He wanted more and more of the thing that he could never get enough of, which was that feeling of being held, that feeling of acceptance. He wanted respect. He wanted passion. He wanted to be wanted. But he could never feel wanted enough. He began to realize that there was not enough attention in the world to satisfy him. 



The young man, who was not especially young anymore, could feel himself crumbling. He struggled to hold form. He went for three mile runs, forcing himself out on the road with the voice of Drill Sergeant Hilliard in his head. “Get the fuck up, son! Put your fucking shoes on! Push yourself up! You’ve got to want this! Go Go Go. Move, Private!” The man pushed himself and pushed himself to stay with the form. He knew what his wife needed from him: security, the nursery, income. He knew what his children needed from him. Or did he know? What he knew about his children is that he needed to be with them. He needed to stay as close to them as he could. He knew that he could not live with himself if he was unable to stay close to them. And so he did.



He felt that his marriage was becoming more and more like a business agreement. His life felt like an obligation. But, he agreed, time after time to shoulder this weight. He agreed, time after time to see what was best in his wife and in his life, although it so often seemed sorely against his very nature. 



He really did learn to truly appreciate his wife’s strengths--the way that she worked in structure and form, the way she taught her students, the way she lead the family down this pragmatic path after Luke had died (that day when he’d thrown his light saber in the corner). 



His wife became his greatest guru. It was she who held him closest. He relied on her. She was his compass, his standard for being. He took in her wisdom and did his best to value her vision. He agreed to meet her standards as best he could. He agreed to study under her great strength, to allow her to define so much of reality for him, and because of this the man grew and learned and experienced a life that he would have never had if he had married someone very much like himself. But, it often did not feel like his life.



“What happened there mother?” the middle-aged-man asked, “Was I giving myself away? Was I living? How often was I happy? How true is this story I’m telling? Am I still trying to understand if I feel like I deserved to be left? Am I still justifying myself in the telling of this story? Am I looking at the things I did right and wrong to justify? Or, am I taking a compassionate look at my life? Hey, have you tricked me into doing another fourth step, Mother? Is this another fearless and searching moral inventory? Is that what’s happening here?”



“Peace, Son,” Continue in your work. Know that I am shining on you. Know that we are together. I am caring for you, my Son. Can you see how I have cared for you throughout your whole life? I know that you can see that, my son.”



“Yes, Great Mother. I can see that. I do see your care in my life. I see your care in all our lives. I see your care in the life of the mother of my children. I see your care in the lives of my children. I want to trust you, Great Mother. Fill me with your presence. Help me to sense you, Dear Mother.”



“You are loved, Son. You are not alone,” she cooed.



Teaching at the college inspired him to go back to school himself. He studied so that he could treat patients at a physical therapy clinic. He continued teaching and performing, but he was still unhappy. Still sick in the great wanting-of-more. 



“Why can’t you just be content,” the wife’s question rang in his ears. The man did not know why he could not be content. He worked on contentedness. He was developing a spiritual practice, but he was still often restless, irritable, and discontent.



The man struggled with depression, sometimes resigning to sit in front of the TV in the evenings for weeks at a time. The man was smoking marijuana because it made him feel hopeful. He prayed when he got high. He was phasing in and out of life, struggling to say “yes,” using whatever worked at the moment, much like he continues to do today as he writes these words.



One night, as the family walked in the door, returning from a dance recital, their great Shepherd, Hope, raised her head and smacked the youngest daughter in the chin. The man became violent. He wished to kill the dog. He planned to grab the dog and strangle her. He had decided to kill the dog. As the man raged, the wife gathered the dog and the children and locked themselves behind a door. 



The man approached the locked door, his sense of alienation at a peak, his arms were raised to beat on the door. He would smash the door. He would scare everyone in the room that had isolated him out here in the living room where he stood all by himself. His raised his arms as he approached the door. He stopped. He saw that he was the abuser now. He saw that he was the father that he hated. He had become the great Clown. Instead of beating on the door, he said “yes” to that death. He lowered his arms and retreated. Defeated. Oh the great distance he still must crawl through that great tunnel of sacred shit!



It was then that he met Penny. Penny, the woman who introduced him to his Pema. The woman who introduced him to unconditional-positive-regard (Hello Mr. Rogers!). Penny, the lesbian that he fell in love with, the one who mothered him, the one who witnessed his tears, his desperate tears that felt like a wall of shame and disgust, a wall that he was unable to maneuver around, a wall that he could not climb over, a wall that he could not crush with his fists. When he hit this wall he cried until he could no longer breathe. He was paralyzed here. Unable to move past. He sat on Penny’s couch and cried and cried. He began a long process of releasing the trauma that had turned him into the very monster that he despised. He found that he really enjoyed opening up in the therapy room. He enjoyed the feeling of vulnerabitly. Penny created for him a safe enviroment.



As he realized how hurting he truly was, he integrated marijuana into his every day life. He attempted to respect the marijuana as a medicine. He went back to school. He became more disciplined. He left the marijuana. He graduated from school. He went back to the medicine. 



He felt that he was so often desperately patching himself back together again. His life was an inflatable life raft, always springing holes, and he was always patching those holes, hoping that the sharks wouldn’t circle around him again. 



Death and rebirth. He reinvented himself dozens of times. Always in the resurrection, hoping that there would not be another death, but another death always followed. The pain. The self loathing. The trauma continued to surface.



Penny told the man that he was one of the “top five self bludgeoners” that she had ever met. The man could now see, in his own heart, how deeply this hate ran him. He was unwilling to beat down the door. He was unable to abuse the dogs any more. The hate had to go somewhere, so as a public service of sorts he directed the hate inward on himself. This is all that he knew to do. This self-hate that would eventually destroy him. The hate that would, again and again lead him to his death. The hate that would lead him to a deeper and still deeper experience.



And so it came to pass that the man was journeying inward, toward the source, toward the One-ess, toward a deeper and deeper salvation, toward a Deeper Power, a Higher Power, making friends with the Snake, slowly reconciling himself to the Christ that was being born in his own being, slowly making peace with God, Slowly making peace with the great What-Is, the I AM-ness. 



And now, as the writer sat on his bed, one day after Christmas, his story continued to emerge before him. These words emerged from this middle-aged-man who was still in desperate search for his salvation. This mother, this father, this artist, this friend, this man who was trying to give himself away to something bigger than himself, this man who was saying yes and still trying to save his own life. So it came to pass that the prayer continued to go forth from his being, calling out to the only One that could help him to die well. The One that he had forsaken. The Self that he had walked away from.



“Please mother,” prayed the middle aged man, “Please hold me. Please don’t let me miss this. Please open my heart. Please help me to feel your love in my being. Please care for me.” 



And so it came to pass that the witer closed his laptop, plugged it in to charge, and started the business of preparing for a trip to Oklahoma City. Tomorrow, if everything went as planned, he would drive East with his children to see both his mother and father. 



The man had watched this trip approaching for weeks now. And this is the story of how the man said “yes” to whatever was to come. This was the next moment in which he surrendered himself. He sang songs of praise with the guitar in his hand. And he loved the (his) cat Eli. 



So it was that he accepted the gift of this room in the impressive adobe house. Please know, dear reader, that he found comfort in your Presence. He took comfort in you that he may never know. 



He said yes to the death and resurrection process. He allowed the words to keep coming from his curled fingers, even as his laptop was closed, not knowing what the exact purpose of these words. 



He clung to this form. He clung to these words that you read now. He gave them his greatest attention, trusting that the Mother and Father were doing a healing work in his being.



He clung to form while releasing his life. He said yes to whatever hidden lessons the medicine had shown him. He gave deep thanks and made his words an offering. He asked that these words would become a prayer for his healing and the healing of all who might find communion in the altar that he was constructing here, this altar of his life, which would hopefully communicate the great message of the Universal Christ and the great Mother and Father.



May all who approach this altar, may all who find shelter here in these words, please join the dying author in his prayer for the Great Turning. May a deeper vision manifest itself in every being who communes here. May these words do there part to bring together a great Union, a great gathering of those who were beyond reach. May these words touch those who are imprisoned and unable to commune with the grass and the soil. May there arise from within us, dear reader, a great healing. May there be a great coming together. A great re-membering. Ring the bells for the great assembly! The second coming of Christ. The birth of the Christ Daughter!



And so it is that I leave you, once again, dear reader. My beloved. I am the one who demands no attention. The one you will forsake three times even before the cock crows. That’s okay. That’s the way of life. For you, I have unconditional positive regard. For you I have the deepest acceptance and love. For you I will give all of my being. 



Please, God

Allow this to arise from deep within us all



Amen

Selah



Hands together

Thumbs on forehead

Bowed toward the deepest heart in all gratitude and Praise
